title: 'I live with a ghost': Japan's haunted homes attract bargain hunters
content_c:
'I live with a ghost': Japan's haunted homes attract bargain hunters
- Published
From the moment Ryua first walked into her rental apartment in Tokyo she believed it to be haunted.
"When I visited the place for a viewing there was a man standing there, glaring at me," she says.
"Since the estate agent couldn't see him, I realised he must be a ghost."
While someone more squeamish would probably have quickly left the flat never to return, Ryua chose to go ahead and move in.
"I'm a bit of a contrarian, so I decided I wanted to become friends with this glaring male ghost," adds Ryua, who works as an aidoru, a young entertainer, and who doesn't wish to share her surname.
Four years later, and still in the same apartment, she says she continues to experience paranormal activity on a daily basis. She says she hears endless footsteps and the ghost talking.
Although Japan has increasingly marked Halloween, external in recent years, many Japanese people take ghosts seriously all year round. The country has a word, "yuurei", which means a lingering, troubled spirit.
These are the ghosts of people who died in violent or tragic circumstances - those who were murdered, killed themselves, or simply were lonely and died alone. If they died at home, then the belief is that their yuurei won't go away.
For house hunters who are not superstitious or squeamish it means there are big bargains to be found. There is a whole category of dwellings called jiko bukken, which means "stigmatised" or "incident" properties.
Under guidelines issued by the government in 2021, Japanese estate agents must disclose suicide, murder, death by fire, and any death where the body was not discovered for an extended period of time.
For rental properties this information must be disclosed for three years, and it must be revealed indefinitely for any property offered for sale.
By contrast, in the UK there is no legal requirement, external to reveal that a person died in a property. And in the US, it differs from state to state., external For example, in California you have to reveal if a person has died in the property in the past three years, while in Arizona and Oregon you do not.
Ryua was told that a man had killed himself in her apartment. It meant that she gets an almost 30% discount on her rent on her tiny, 25 sq m bedsit in the fashionable ward of Setagaya. She says she pays 45,000 yen ($285; £213) a month, instead of what should have been 62,000 yen.
While a house where there had been a murder or suicide would probably be harder to sell or rent out anywhere in the world, Tokyo estate agent Erik Oskamp says that Japanese people are particularly superstitious and averse to stigmatised properties.
"[Even] an apartment next to a cemetery will be difficult to rent out, especially if you can see the tombs from the kitchen," explains Oskamp. "The worst thing is if a suicide has happened in the apartment. Even if somebody has jumped from the roof, many renters will move out. Other issues are a serious crime or a lonely death."
The latter issue, that of a person dying alone, would not generally affect the price of a property in, say, the UK or the US.
But in rural Kagoshima, in Japan's southwest, it enabled Diane Tincher to buy a large three-bedroom house for about half of what would have otherwise been the asking price.
'If there is a ghost I'm thankful to her'
The 79-year-old American has lived in Japan for nearly 40 years, working as a tour guide. She says that the estate agent had been straight with her – there was a heavy discount as an elderly lady had died alone, thereby stigmatising the property.
Tincher paid 20m yen for the house, in a location where similar properties usually sell for up to 45m yen.
"I don't believe in ghosts. But I know that the Japanese are very superstitious," she says. "If there is a ghost I'm thankful to her every day... to live in such a splendid and affordable home."
Researching the house, Tincher had found it on a website called Oshimaland, which lists jiko bukken properties, giving details of the events that occurred. It was launched in 2005 covering Tokyo, before expanding across Japan and then internationally in 2011.
It is crowdsourced, meaning that members of the public add the homes and their details.
Teru Oshima, the founder of Oshimaland, says that in the past such properties were "not very attractive options" in Japan.
Yet as house prices have surged in the country in recent years, as well as a big increase in the wider cost of living, one 2025 survey found that more than half of Japanese people would now rent a jiko bukken if it was cheap., external
Back in Setagaya, Ryua says she is happy living with her ghostly flatmate. "I believe that ghosts were once living human beings, so they deserve our respect," she says.

title: EU backs away from offer to Canada to start ‘associate member’ talks
content_c:
The EU has backed away from its offer to Canada to start talks on becoming an “associate member” after disagreements between members states just as an EU-Canada summit was set to begin in Montreal.
A draft of a joint statement to be issued after the end of the summit, which runs Thursday and Friday, showed a watered-down version offering “an ever closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership itself”.
The issue was triggered after the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, surprised nearly everyone by announcing in last month’s state of the union address that the EU would consider “associate membership” for Canada.
The declaration had been hailed as a landmark in EU history, offering a non-EU country such close ties to the bloc, which has not allowed any state membership since Croatia joined in 2013.
It was also seen as a sign that the call by Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, at the Davos summit in January for “middle powers” to work together was paying off.
But instead of announcing a work programme on developing “associate membership”, the draft communique, seen by the Guardian, states the two sides would “work to define by the 2027 EU-Canada summit the concept of an ever closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership itself, to reflect, through this even closer association, our common endeavour and cooperation towards our shared goals of prosperity, economic security and strategic autonomy”.
Associate membership had been mooted, and rejected, previously for countries such as Ukraine.
Von der Leyen’s declaration caught EU capitals by surprise and led to pushback politically and legally. Given “associate status” has no definition, diplomats wondered about such issues as whether Canada could join the European Council, legislative bodies or decision-making processes without a vote.
At a meeting on Monday, ambassadors in the EU raised concerns about the dramatic offer, but vowed to make efforts to seek a diplomatic path to rescinding the offer of “associate” membership without embarrassing Von der Leyen. It is understood that Italy suggested “associate membership as proposed by the commission”, with the definition to be thrashed out later by member states.
Germany walked back further, suggesting the wording “an ever closer association of Canada” to the EU.
“Nobody was consulted about associate membership apart from [Von der Leyen’s] closest staff, it would seem. Many member states, including Germany, were not happy. This is all about fixing the plane while it is flying,” said one diplomat.
Germany had argued that “associate membership” should be reserved as an interim step for prospective candidate countries, such as Ukraine or Montenegro, noting that the status has no formal grounding in current EU treaties.
Donald Trump, the US president, previously called the EU’s proposal to make Canada an associate member “laughable”, and said if he interpreted the move as a “hostile act” the US might stop trading with Europe “on many things”.
A bitter trade war with the US, a longtime ally, has seen Carney seek out new trading partnerships around the world. Ahead of the summit in Montreal, one of Canada’s largest banks released a report suggesting there was “meaningful” upside for Canada if it were to deepen economic ties with Europe. Tens of billions of dollars in additional trade would be possible if barriers were removed in areas of overlapping interest such as defence, energy, critical minerals and digital markets, TD Economics said.
Carney has spoken specifically about the need to lessen reliance on Elon Musk‘s Starlink satellite network, following a decision to throttle its usage over Ukraine.
Earlier this week, Carney posted on social media that Canada would join the popular music competition Eurovision. But despite fears raised by political rivals, Carney has said Canada has no interest in formally joining the EU. Changing Canadian laws to bring it in line with European nations would probably prove unpopular, despite public support for stronger ties.
Carney told reporters on Tuesday that the summit this week was the launch of further formal negotiations that will take place another year.
“The good news is it doesn’t matter about specific names or nomenclature,” Carney said. “What matters is the difference it will make to the lives of Canadians.”
A previous draft statement had included at least two references to Canada as an “associate member”, including an acknowledgment that defining the term would take another year.

title: EU countries block Canada's 'associate membership' plan
content_c:
EU countries block Canada's 'associate membership' plan
October 29, 2026
European Union member states have blocked a proposal by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to grant Canada a special status as an "associate member" of the bloc.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and several other EU leaders pushed to remove the term from a draft declaration ahead of a two-day EU-Canada summit beginning Thursday in Montreal, according to diplomats cited by the dpa and AFP news agencies.
Instead, the revised document calls for a plan to establish "closer ties" between Canada and the EU without membership.
The declaration was approved by EU member states on Wednesday evening and is expected to be published on Friday, at the end of the summit.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, von der Leyen, European Council President Antonio Costa and several EU commissioners are attending the talks.
Why did EU countries oppose Canada's associate membership?
Von der Leyen first proposed making Canada the EU's first "associate member" in September during a speech attended by Carney.
However, the proposal raised questions among member states because existing EU treaties do not provide for such a status.
Diplomats said several governments were concerned about the lack of clarity surrounding the proposed arrangement and insufficient consultation between the European Commission and EU member states.
Germany, France and Italy were among the countries that raised objections, although they broadly support closer cooperation with Canada.
Another concern was that the term "associate membership" had already been used in discussions about Ukraine's potential accession to the EU.
Merz had previously suggested such a status for Ukraine as an intermediate step toward full membership. Under his proposal, Kyiv could participate in EU summits and ministerial meetings without voting rights.
Von der Leyen, however, used the same term to describe a different arrangement for Canada, a country that does not have a legal path to EU membership.
An earlier draft of the summit declaration would have allowed Canada to participate in consultations on major EU political and regulatory initiatives as an associate member.
It also called for the full scope of the arrangement to be defined by the 2027 EU-Canada summit.
Carney, meanwhile, played down the dispute over the wording of the summit declaration.
He said the precise terminology mattered less than the practical benefits closer cooperation would bring to Canadians.
What will closer EU-Canada cooperation involve?
Despite the disagreement over terminology, both sides intend to significantly deepen their partnership.
The revised declaration focuses on an "Alliance for the Future," a term Carney has frequently used to describe relations between Canada and the EU.
The initiative aims to remove trade barriers, facilitate investment and secure supplies of critical raw materials, medicines and technologies during crises.
Both sides also want to strengthen cooperation on energy, climate protection, artificial intelligence, security and education.
Canada could gain broader access to EU programs covering research, education and defense.
A new economic council is planned to bring together businesses from both sides of the Atlantic.
The declaration also calls for a study into the feasibility of increasing Canadian liquefied natural gas exports to Europe.
However, EU governments watered down several economic commitments in the original draft.
An explicit goal of deeper financial market integration was removed. Instead of promising preferential treatment in economic security measures, both sides now intend to limit potential negative effects on each other.
How has Donald Trump affected EU-Canada relations?
The push for closer ties comes amid growing uncertainty over relations with the United States under President Donald Trump.
Trade disputes, US tariffs and Trump's territorial claims have raised concerns in both Canada and Europe about Washington's reliability as a partner.
Both sides hope that closer cooperation will help reduce their dependence on other countries and strengthen their ability to pursue common interests.
Trump previously dismissed the idea of Canadian associate membership in the EU as ridiculous.
He also threatened consequences if the arrangement harmed US interests, warning that he could impose high tariffs or halt trade with Europe in several sectors.
Edited by: Sean Sinico

Von der Leyen first proposed making Canada the EU's first "associate member" in September during a speech attended by Carney.
However, the proposal raised questions among member states because existing EU treaties do not provide for such a status.
Diplomats said several governments were concerned about the lack of clarity surrounding the proposed arrangement and insufficient consultation between the European Commission and EU member states.
Germany, France and Italy were among the countries that raised objections, although they broadly support closer cooperation with Canada.
Another concern was that the term "associate membership" had already been used in discussions about Ukraine's potential accession to the EU.
Merz had previously suggested such a status for Ukraine as an intermediate step toward full membership. Under his proposal, Kyiv could participate in EU summits and ministerial meetings without voting rights.
Von der Leyen, however, used the same term to describe a different arrangement for Canada, a country that does not have a legal path to EU membership.
An earlier draft of the summit declaration would have allowed Canada to participate in consultations on major EU political and regulatory initiatives as an associate member.
It also called for the full scope of the arrangement to be defined by the 2027 EU-Canada summit.
Carney, meanwhile, played down the dispute over the wording of the summit declaration.
He said the precise terminology mattered less than the practical benefits closer cooperation would bring to Canadians.
What will closer EU-Canada cooperation involve?
Despite the disagreement over terminology, both sides intend to significantly deepen their partnership.
The revised declaration focuses on an "Alliance for the Future," a term Carney has frequently used to describe relations between Canada and the EU.
The initiative aims to remove trade barriers, facilitate investment and secure supplies of critical raw materials, medicines and technologies during crises.
Both sides also want to strengthen cooperation on energy, climate protection, artificial intelligence, security and education.
Canada could gain broader access to EU programs covering research, education and defense.
A new economic council is planned to bring together businesses from both sides of the Atlantic.
The declaration also calls for a study into the feasibility of increasing Canadian liquefied natural gas exports to Europe.
However, EU governments watered down several economic commitments in the original draft.
An explicit goal of deeper financial market integration was removed. Instead of promising preferential treatment in economic security measures, both sides now intend to limit potential negative effects on each other.
How has Donald Trump affected EU-Canada relations?
The push for closer ties comes amid growing uncertainty over relations with the United States under President Donald Trump.
Trade disputes, US tariffs and Trump's territorial claims have raised concerns in both Canada and Europe about Washington's reliability as a partner.
Both sides hope that closer cooperation will help reduce their dependence on other countries and strengthen their ability to pursue common interests.
Trump previously dismissed the idea of Canadian associate membership in the EU as ridiculous.
He also threatened consequences if the arrangement harmed US interests, warning that he could impose high tariffs or halt trade with Europe in several sectors.

title: Zugunglück in Spanien: Der Schock sitzt tief
content_c:
Zugunglück in Spanien Der Schock sitzt tief
In Spanien sitzt der Schock tief über das zweite schwere Zugunglück auf der Hochgeschwindigkeitszugstrecke zwischen Madrid und Andalusien. Mindestens 68 Menschen verloren bei dem Unglück in der Region Toledo ihr Leben.
Mittwochabend 20 Uhr - Spanien schweigt. Eine Schweigeminute in Madrid, in Barcelona im Nordosten des Landes, wie auch in Sevilla im Südwesten und in Adamuz - erst vor zehn Monaten starben hier 46 Menschen bei einem Hochgeschwindigkeitszugunglück.
In Urda bei Toledo, dem aktuellen Unglücksort: Sprachlosigkeit, Fassungslosigkeit, Trauer.
Ein Land sucht Trost
Urda ist ein kleiner Ort mit knapp zweieinhalbtausend Einwohnern in der Region Toledo. Hier versucht am Nachmittag der Priester José Manuel Pastrana, den Schrecken in Worte zu fassen. Der Seelsorger war seit 10 Uhr morgens an der Unglücksstelle. Er beschreibt die Situation als unfassbar: "Mit Schwerverletzten, mit Verletzten, die Trost suchten. Menschen, die aus nicht betroffenen Waggons ausstiegen. Die hatten zwar keinen körperlichen, aber einen enormen seelischen Schmerz angesichts des Ausmaßes einer Tragödie, die einfach erschütternd ist."
Erschüttert ist auch Tangui Binier. Er sagt, er sei Stammgast auf der Strecke, saß im Zug des privaten Unternehmens Iryo, der nach einem Ausfall des Sicherheitssystems auf freier Strecke stand, auf den dann ein zweiter Zug mit hoher Geschwindigkeit auffuhr. "Da waren Menschen, die eingeklemmt waren, Menschen mit schrecklichen und allen denkbaren Verletzungen. Es war furchtbar, ehrlich gesagt eine sehr harte Erfahrung. Aber ich danke all denen, die uns geholfen haben." So etwas dürfe in Spanien nicht passieren, fügt er hinzu.
Anlaufstelle für Betroffene
Weiter oben im Ort ist die Umgebung einer Schule abgesperrt, drinnen wandern Menschen umher, die nach Angehörigen suchen. Betreut unter anderem von Mitarbeitern des Roten Kreuzes wie Daniel Losada: "Letztlich ist das als zentrale Anlaufstelle für Angehörige gedacht, eine Informationsstelle, wo die Dienste zusammengefasst sind, die sie unterstützen und ihnen hoffentlich auch ein wenig emotionale Sicherheit geben können."
Etwa Menschen, denen es bisher nicht gelungen sei, Kontakt zu vermissten Angehörigen aufzunehmen. Viele Personen seien direkt evakuiert und in Krankenhäuser oder Gesundheitszentren gebracht worden. Es sei derzeit kompliziert und manchmal sehr schwierig, Kontakt zu Menschen aufzunehmen, die sich in einem Krankenhaus befänden.
Auf das Leid der Angehörigen geht auch Spaniens Ministerpräsident Pedro Sánchez bei seinem Besuch an der Unglücksstelle ein. Die spanische Gesellschaft teile ihren Schmerz, erklärt Sánchez, und steht dabei nur gut 250 Kilometer nördlich der Stelle auf derselben Strecke, wo bei einem ähnlichen Unglück im Januar 46 Menschen ihr Leben verloren hatten. "Wir haben auf den Hochgeschwindigkeitsstrecken zwei schreckliche Tragödien in einem Jahr erlebt. Vieles deutet bisher darauf hin, dass die Ursachen der beiden Unfälle in keinem Zusammenhang stehen."
Ursachenforschung läuft
Die Ursachenforschung läuft, Sánchez verspricht gründliche Aufklärung. Derzeit deutet vieles auf menschliches Versagen hin, aber für ein abschließendes Urteil ist es noch zu früh.
Vorerst gilt: suchen, bergen, versorgen - Rettungskräfte arbeiten die Nacht durch. Darunter Angehörige der Katastrophenschutzeinheit des spanischen Militärs, Hunderte Polizisten, mehrere große Kräne sind im Einsatz. Außerdem auch Drohnen mit Wärmebildsensoren und eine Hundestaffel, um Menschen in den Trümmern aufzuspüren.
Die Arbeiten dürften nicht innerhalb weniger Tage abgeschlossen sein. Das staatliche Bahnunternehmen Renfe hat den Fahrkartenverkauf für Hochgeschwindigkeitszüge zwischen Madrid und Andalusien zunächst bis Dezember ausgesetzt.
In Spanien gilt nun drei Tage Staatstrauer, doch bis der Schmerz auch nur ansatzweise verflogen ist, dürfte deutlich mehr Zeit vergehen. Wenn er überhaupt jemals verfliegt.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro flieht nach Wahlniederlage aus Brasilien
content_c:
Flávio Bolsonaro flieht nach Wahlniederlage aus Brasilien
Veröffentlicht 28. Oktober 2026Zuletzt aktualisiert 28. Oktober 2026
Wenige Tage nach seiner Niederlage bei der Präsidentschaftswahl in Brasilien ist der rechte Kandidat Flávio Bolsonaro trotz eines richterlichen Ausreiseverbots außer Landes geflohen. Laut der argentinischen Einwanderungsbehörde reiste der Senator auf dem Landweg in das Nachbarland ein und flog mit einem Privatflugzeug Richtung Ecuador. Von dort aus nahm die Maschine Kurs auf die USA; inzwischen landete sie in Miami im Bundesstaat Florida.
US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte nach Berichten über eine Flucht des brasilianischen Politikers dessen mögliche Einreise in der Nacht zu Mittwoch begrüßt. Zugleich kritisierte er die Wahl in Brasilien als "schrecklich", ohne dies näher zu begründen. Schon zuvor hatte ein US-Beamter bestätigt, Bolsonaro und dessen Angehörigen würden Visa gewährt.
Ermittlungen wegen Geldwäsche
Vor seiner Ausreise war der Politiker einer Anordnung des Obersten Gerichts in Brasilien vom Montag nicht nachgekommen, seine Reisepässe binnen 24 Stunden abzugeben. Der in rechten Kreisen angefeindete Richter Alexandre de Moraes hatte Bolsonaros Pässe für ungültig erklärt und diesem untersagt, das Land zu verlassen. Die Verfügung wurde im Rahmen eines Ermittlungsverfahrens gegen Bolsonaro und den Anwalt Willer Tomaz erlassen. Dabei geht es um mutmaßliche Geldwäsche im Zusammenhang mit Unternehmen und Online-Sportwetten.
In den vergangenen Tagen hatte Bolsonaro noch beteuert, er wolle seine Pässe abgeben; allerdings werde er sich gegen die aus seiner Sicht ungerechtfertigte Maßnahme wehren. Er bestritt jegliche Ausreisepläne. Der 45-Jährige führte die Anordnung des Gerichts auf eine Äußerung seines seit 2025 in den USA lebenden Bruders Eduardo zurück. Dieser hatte vor der Wahl eine Ausreise Flávios im Fall einer Niederlage gegen Amtsinhaber Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva befürwortet.
Gegen Eduardo Bolsonaro, der ebenfalls Politiker in seinem Heimatland war, liegt dort ein Haftbefehl vor. Er hatte während des Strafprozesses gegen seinen Vater wiederholt auf Sanktionen Washingtons gegen Richter des Obersten Gerichts gedrängt.
Vater verbüßt Haftstrafe im Hausarrest
Der 71-jährige Jair Bolsonaro verbüßt derzeit im Hausarrest eine 27-jährige Haftstrafe, zu der er wegen Beteiligung an einem versuchten Staatsstreich verurteilt worden war. Er wurde auch mit einem Ämterverbot belegt, weshalb sein Sohn Flávio an seine Stelle trat.
Noch ehe dessen Flucht offiziell bestätigt wurde, hatte Präsident Lula die mutmaßlichen Pläne seines Rivalen kritisiert. "Ich frage mich, welche Schuld ein Bürger auf dem Gewissen hat, der gerade die Wahl verloren hat und aus seinem Land flieht", sagte Lula bei einer Feier zu seinem 81. Geburtstag im Präsidentenpalast.
Bolsonaro, dessen Vater Jair das Land von 2019 bis 2023 regiert hatte, war bei der Stichwahl um das Präsidentenamt am Sonntag dem Amtsinhaber Lula da Silva unterlegen. Er erhielt dem offiziellen Ergebnis zufolge 48,2 Prozent der Stimmen; Lula kam auf 51,8 Prozent der Stimmen. Anders als Bolsonaro selbst hat seine rechte Partei den Wahlsieg des linken Amtsinhabers ausdrücklich anerkannt.
Der unterlegene Kandidat teilte am Montag mit, er werde Lulas Wahlkampfführung juristisch prüfen lassen. Damit wollte er erreichen, dass der Präsident und dessen Vize Geraldo Alckmin wegen angeblichen Missbrauchs politischer und wirtschaftlicher Macht im Wahlkampf nicht für eine neue Amtszeit vereidigt werden dürfen.
jj/haz (dpa, afp, rtr)
Redaktionsschluss: 17.30 Uhr (MESZ) - dieser Artikel wird nicht weiter aktualisiert.

title: До Києва суне нове похолодання: синоптики назвали дати, коли температура почне різко падати — детальний прогноз
content_c:
До Києва суне нове похолодання: синоптики назвали дати, коли температура почне різко падати — детальний прогноз
Попри дощову та хмарну погоду 29 жовтня, стовпчики термометрів у столиці ще утримаються на позначці близько +10 градусів.
У Києві 29 жовтня утримається відносно тепла осіння погода з можливим дощем.
За словами синоптикині Наталки Діденко у Києві 29 жовтня істотних опадів не передбачається, денна температура повітря коливатиметься в межах від +10 до +12 градусів тепла.
«Логічне пізньоосіннє похолодання розпочнеться із початком листопада», — зазначає синоптикиня.
В Українському гідрометцентрі повідомляють, що 29 жовтня по території Київщини та міста Києва буде хмарно з проясненнями, також будуть дощі. Вітер дутиме північно-східний та зі швидкістю 7-12 м/с. title: 146 экспертов призвали признать изменение климата чрезвычайной ситуацией в сфере здравоохранения
content_c:
Международная группа ученых в рамках проекта The Lancet Countdown 2026 («Обратный отсчет The Lancet: здоровье и изменение климата») призвала признать изменения климата чрезвычайной ситуацией в сфере здравоохранения. Они отмечают, что рекордная жара препятствует работе, перегружает больницы и уносит тысячи жизней по всему миру, сообщает Science Alert.
В докладе отмечается, что риски и негативные последствия, связанные с экстремальной жарой и засухами, растут быстрее, чем принимаемые меры по борьбе с изменением климата — несмотря на то, что за последнее десятилетие значительно увеличились инвестиции в переход от ископаемого топлива к другим источникам энергии.
«Темпы роста многих угроз здоровью, связанных с климатом, ускоряются; число смертей от жары, обусловленных изменением климата, достигло рекордного уровня, а экономический ущерб тяжелее всего сказывается на наиболее уязвимых секторах экономики и группах населения», — заявила исполнительный директор проекта The Lancet Countdown Марина Романелло, исследователь в области климата и здоровья.
Прошло 10 лет с момента публикации первого доклада Countdown, в работе над которым приняли участие эксперты в области общественного здравоохранения, климата, энергетики, анализа данных, экономики и других сфер. Цель проекта — отслеживать влияние изменения климата на 54 показателя здоровья.
Авторы нового доклада обеспокоены тем, как медленно международное сообщество внедряет изменения, необходимые для сохранения здоровья людей.
«Спустя 10 лет после принятия Парижского соглашения наши выводы однозначны: вред для здоровья, вызванный изменением климата, растет быстрее, чем принимаемые в мире ответные меры, а во многих случаях этот процесс даже ускоряется. Достигнут реальный прогресс в таких областях, как переход на экологически чистую энергию, повышение готовности систем здравоохранения и принятие нормативных актов, направленных на охрану здоровья. Все это уже приносит пользу местным сообществам. Но прогресс идет слишком медленно, он недостаточно значителен и не доходит до тех, кто нуждается в нем больше всего. Именно поэтому мы призываем официально признать изменение климата глобальной чрезвычайной ситуацией в области здравоохранения, поставив вопросы здоровья в центр любого решения, касающегося климата», — отметила Романелло.
В 2023 году 71,5% смертей, связанных с жарой, по всему миру можно было объяснить изменением климата. Всего таких смертей было 710 тысяч. По оценкам, если бы не изменение климата, это число составило бы около 200 тысяч. В период с 2016 по 2023 год ежегодно фиксировалось в среднем 540 800 смертей, связанных с воздействием жары. На долю изменения климата пришлось 68% этих случаев (369 900) — это значительный рост по сравнению с предыдущим десятилетием (2006–2015 гг.), когда этот показатель составлял 55%.
В 2025 году жара привела к потерям в мировой экономической производительности в размере около 1,07 триллиона долларов США — исключительно из-за того, что она препятствовала нормальной трудовой деятельности людей. Наиболее существенные потери ВВП были отмечены в странах Юго-Восточной Азии и Африки.
В мировом масштабе сельское хозяйство и строительство особенно сильно пострадали от потерь, связанных с жарой, поскольку эти отрасли зависят от труда людей, выполняющих тяжелую физическую работу на открытом воздухе.
У человеческого организма есть свои пределы, а условия на улице все чаще становятся невыносимыми — если не смертельно опасными.
Напомним, в конце июня запад Европы охватила рекордная жара, тогда в странах региона было зафиксировано более 10 тысяч случаев избыточных смертей. По данным сети EuroMOMO, более девяти тысяч из них пришлись на людей в возрасте от 65 лет.

title: Доглядала за тваринами 40 років і померла від укусів леопарда
content_c:
Доглядала за тваринами 40 років і померла від укусів леопарда
  - Author, Олівія Айрленд
- Published
- Час прочитання: 2 хв
Працівниця нідерландського зоопарку померла після нападу леопарда, підтвердило керівництво сафарі-парку Beekse Bergen. Жінка пропрацювала в парку 40 років.
Інцидент стався у суботу, коли співробітниця парку доглядала у вольєрі за двома перськими леопардами.
Вона зазнала тяжких травм голови та шиї й перенесла невідкладну операцію, однак у вівторок парк повідомив про її смерть.
Адміністрація заявила, що обставини інциденту розслідуватиме незалежна комісія.
За повідомленням парку Beekse Bergen на півдні Нідерландів, жінка почала працювати там у 17 років і з перервами присвятила цьому місцю чотири десятиліття.
"Її смерть глибоко вразила всіх нас. Ми висловлюємо щирі співчуття її родині, друзям і близьким. Нині наш пріоритет – підтримка родини та колег", – йдеться в заяві.
Двох леопардів зазвичай тримають окремо від персоналу, але через погоду їх перевели у вольєр.
Що саме там сталося, поки що невідомо, оскільки всередині немає камер відеоспостереження.
За даними місцевого видання NL Times, попри тяжкі поранення жінка змогла викликати колег по рації. Згодом її у критичному стані доправили до лікарні гелікоптером.
Речник парку повідомив місцевому мовнику Omroep Brabant, що леопарди поводилися відповідно до своєї природи, тому присипляти їх не будуть.
"Вони є і залишаються хижаками", – зазначив він.
У Beekse Bergen також повідомили, що облаштують місце пам'яті, де відвідувачі та працівники зможуть залишити слова співчуття.

title: Сумщина спрямувала 2,4 млн грн на станції керування дронами для 8-го корпусу ДШВ – Григоров
content_c:
З обласного бюджету Сумщини спрямували 2,4 млн грн на придбання чотирьох комплектів станцій керування безпілотниками для бійців 8-го корпусу Десантно-штурмових військ, повідомив начальник Сумської ОВА Олег Григоров.
"Ця допомога – результат прямої комунікації з військовими та реагування на їхні потреби. І цю роботу ми продовжуємо системно", – написав він у телеграмі.
За словами Григорова, перший комплект обладнання вже надійшов і військові беруть його в роботу. Він допомагатиме підрозділу ефективніше виконувати завдання з протиповітряної оборони та розвідки.
Обладнання закупили на запит бійців корпусу.

title: How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
content_c:
How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
- Published
Israel looks to be in political deadlock.
With 85% of votes counted after Tuesday's election, neither the incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, nor the bloc of his key challenger Gadi Eisenkot look set to win a majority.
In order to form a government, it looks likely one of the leading parties would have to break their campaign promises - meaning the most probable outcome may well be new elections.
Here are four possible scenarios.
National unity government led by Netanyahu
Could Netanyahu persuade Eisenkot to join him in a national unity government?
Eisenkot would have to abandon his key platform to do so. He's framed himself as the only alternative to Netanyahu, and built his campaign on ousting him from power.
Just last night, he took to the stage at his campaign HQ and called on Netanyahu to "announce his retirement from political life today," telling the crowd that Israelis are fed up with Netanyahu's "culture of lies", "division and incitement".
But that was before one of the main exit polls - which had initially projected a lead for Eisenkot's bloc - was revised, and he was overtaken by Netanyahu.
Netanyahu could try to persuade Eisenkot's Yashar Party to join his Likud Party in a unity government by ditching the far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties he is currently in coalition with. But last night at Likud HQ he thanked his "loyal partners" and called for a "strong right-wing government" - remarks some have interpreted as meaning he intends to preserve his alliance with them.
One thing that could make a unity government more likely is a renewed conflict with Iran, which could place serious pressure on party leaders to put aside their political differences and work together. In the days prior to the election, Israeli and US media reported that Netanyahu was pushing for fresh strikes on the country, and had pressed Donald Trump to approve US involvement.
This would no-doubt be framed by Netanyahu's critics as an attempt to save his own political skin by entering another regional conflict.

This would be a seismic shift for Israeli politics. Only one independent Arab party has ever formally been part of a coalition, in 2021, and it didn't last long.
Eisenkot and every other Jewish party in his bloc bar one have already ruled out entering government with them. But right now, it's the opposition's only path to a majority.
The Arab parties were the story of election night. They look to have defied expectations and could gain a record 19 seats - helped by an unprecedented turnout from Israel's Arab population, who account for about one-fifth of the country and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel.
For years, many boycotted Israeli elections, saying voting would legitimise a system that they say treats them as second-class citizens. But their turnout last night was inspired by a desire to oust the most right-wing governing coalition in Israel's history.
The United Arab list, who are currently projected to win around 7 seats, have said they'd join an opposition government, while The Joint List, who are projected to win 12 seats, have said they'd support one from outside.
However, the only Jewish leader advocating this scenario right now is The Democrats' Yair Golan. And a coalition like this would be very fragile, especially on issues like Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
The fact there is such a unified front from the otherwise fragmented Jewish parties against Arab participation points to Israel's deep divisions.
Netanyahu-led majority, with right-wingers from opposition
Could Netanyahu persuade the right-wing parties in Eisenkot's bloc to break away and join his coalition?
The two most likely candidates for this are Naftali Bennett - joint-leader of the Beyachad political alliance - and Avigdor Lieberman, leader of the Yisrael Beiteinu party. They are both right-wingers who are hardline on security, and share some political ground with Netanyahu.
But both campaigned explicitly to oust him, and to extend military conscription to the ultra-Orthodox - bringing them into direct conflict with the two ultra-Orthodox parties already part of Netanyahu's government. So it's difficult to see them joining forces.
Some have suggested Bennett and Lieberman's parties could replace the ultra-Orthodox parties, but current electoral math suggests that grouping may not have the seats needed for a majority.

If none of the above scenarios can be negotiated, the default outcome would be new elections.
Many would see this as a tacit win for Netanyahu, who would remain as caretaker PM until the new elections take place - and he may believe he has a better chance of winning them.
Some analysts think the high Arab turnout would not be repeated - especially if their record representation in parliament led to no change. And it could also mobilise more right-wing voters in a second poll.
Netanyahu may also bet that the estimated 70,000 Israelis who flew home from abroad to vote, and are thought to skew against him, wouldn't do so again.
Additionally, several right-wing parties who failed to pass the electoral threshold of 3.25% may attract fewer votes or may not even run, thereby bringing more votes to Likud and its allies.
Between 2019 and 2022, Israel held five separate elections as Netanyahu and his rivals struggled time and again to co-operate.

title: Healey tells departments to make 1% cuts to fund defence
content_c:
Healey tells departments to make 1% cuts to fund defence
- Published
Chancellor John Healey has told every government department to find 1% cuts in their capital budgets to fill a £4.7bn hole in the funding of the Defence Investment Plan.
The reductions come on top of the 1% cuts departments were asked to make earlier this year in order to pay for the initial £10.3bn of the plan's overall £15bn price tag.
The plan boosted defence spending; however the chancellor continues to come under pressure to explain how he will meet a further target of spending 3% of national income on defence by 2030.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused the chancellor of only offering "a plan to have a plan" adding: "I bet [Vladimir] Putin's really scared now."
Setting out his Budget, Healey hinted that meeting that goal would require further cuts, telling MPs it would involve "looking hard at public spending".
He said he would set out how the UK would reach the 3% target by 2030, as well as 3.5% of GDP by 2035, at next year's spending review.
Government departments have yet to decide what will be cut from their capital budgets.
Capital budgets are focused on long-term investments, rather than day-to-day spending. For example, earlier this year, when departments had to make capital budget cuts to fund the initial defence spending rise, a number of major road improvement schemes were scrapped.
Badenoch criticised Healey for not using his Budget to explain how he would boost defence funding to 3%.
"He is the man who is making our country less safe. He has failed his own test. This is on him, and no one will ever forget," she said.
The Conservatives have previously urged the government to pay for defence by making cuts to the welfare budget.
Nato secretary general Mark Rutte said the UK was on "a credible path towards meeting the commitment made by all Nato Allies in The Hague - to ensure we're all investing what's needed to remain ready & able to deter aggression and defend our freedom and security".
Chair of the Commons defence committee - and Labour MP - Tan Dhesi said "some of the key decisions on defence spending have lamentably been delayed until next year's spending review".
He added: "There is a cost to inaction. Investment in our nation's defence and security cannot be kicked into the long grass."
Former Nato secretary general Lord Robertson told the BBC the Budget was "pretty good news for defence generally" but warned there would be "battles ahead with the spending departments" to reach the 3% target.
Earlier this year, Healey resigned as defence secretary, accusing the then-Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer of not providing enough money to keep the UK safe.
In a scathing resignation letter, he specifically emphasised his belief in the importance of reaching a 3% target by 2030.
Now chancellor, Healey told the House of Commons on Wednesday: "At the spending review next year, I confirm that I will set out the details of how we will meet our Nato commitment to spend 3.5% of GDP on defence by 2035, with a target date for 3% in 2030.
"And today, I am getting work under way to get there in a fiscally sustainable way."
In addition to looking at public spending, Healey said he also wanted to use "more innovative financing alongside the private sector and our international allies".
The chancellor said this would include:
- starting treaty negotiations with Finland, Poland and Netherlands to set up a "multilateral defence mechanism" which would allow allies to share resources
- increasing the amount of private investment in defence through public-private partnerships
- directing the National Wealth Fund and British Business Bank to put £5bn into "defence, dual-use technology and sovereign capability"
The Office for Budget Responsibility estimates that the UK government's target to increase defence spending to 3.5% of GDP by 2035 will cost £35bn.
Helen Miller, director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said: "Increasing investment in defence companies may contribute to the target but it is unclear how much this will lead to an increase in UK defence capabilities.
"There is much further to go to get to 3% of GDP on defence and it is hard to believe that this government will want to get there without topping up spending totals."
- Burnham treads carefully with Zelensky visit, balancing Trump and Ukraine 
  - Published14 October
In his Budget speech, Healey also announced £10bn of economic and military support for Ukraine, in the form of loans and export guarantees.
The funding includes £5.5bn of loans through World Bank guarantees and a grant contribution to the World Bank International Development Association's crisis facility.
A further £3bn will be made available to Ukraine through loans facilitated by UK Export Finance, a government export credit agency.
Healey told the House of Commons that the week had started with Russia launching a "brutal ballistic missile attack" and that the extra money would send "a clear message to Moscow".
He said that when he told the Ukrainian leader about the additional support in a phone call, President Volodymyr Zelensky had said: "You've made my day."
Later on social media, Zelensky welcomed the money, saying: "Every step to strengthen Ukraine brings Russia closer to realising that it must end this war of its own making."
The money comes on top of the UK's pledge to provide Ukraine with £3bn of military support until at least 2030-31.

title: Microsoft profits soar days after announcing thousands of layoffs
content_c:
Microsoft profits soar days after announcing thousands of layoffs
- Published
Technology giant Microsoft says its profits for the three months to the end of September jumped to more than $36.6bn (£27.5bn), just days after announcing plans to cut its workforce by more than a quarter.
On Monday, the Windows developer said it would offer buyouts to around 60,000 of its workers to cut costs as it pours billions of dollars into artificial intelligence (AI).
Like many other major tech firms, Microsoft is investing heavily in the infrastructure that powers AI even as questions remain over whether such huge spending will pay off.
Microsoft shares rose by almost 2.9% in after hours trading in New York on Wednesday.
The recent financial results of tech companies have been closely watched by investors as they gauge whether the heavy spending on AI is sustainable.
Big tech companies like Amazon, Meta and Alphabet are expected to spend more than $700bn this year on AI chips and infrastructure like data centres.
Microsoft said on Wednesday that its quarterly revenue rose to $92.3bn - up 19% from a year earlier - driven by strong growth in its cloud computing business.
Its earnings were lifted by a 30% increase in revenue for Microsoft Cloud - its range of enterprise technology services.
The firm also flagged risks, including "substantial investments" in AI, among other uncertainties that could impact its finances.
The firm's chief executive Satya Nadella said AI development has helped grow the adoption of the technology and has delivered "real-world impact across every industry."
This week, the company said it would extend a voluntary redundancy offer to eligible employees in teams across Canada, India, the UK and US to adapt its workforce to "changing needs".
It will create "greater flexibility" for the firm and allow workers to leave with financial support and career planning resources, Microsoft said.
The company currently employs more than 220,000 people around the world.
Microsoft's stronger-than-expected earnings contrasted with Alphabet, as the owner of Google disappointed investors with its financial results on Wednesday.
The firm's shares fell by 9.75% after it reported a 25% drop in quarterly net profit from a year earlier and said it will continue to spend heavily on AI.

title: US ambassador suggests Trump could blame Canada if midterms don’t go his way
content_c:
The US ambassador has suggested Canada could be blamed if Republicans perform poorly in next week’s midterm elections, the latest intervention from a controversial figure who has been accused of inflaming a bitter dispute that has angered and baffled residents of both countries.
On Wednesday, CTV news reported that Pete Hoekstra told business leaders at a closed door meeting that if a number of swing races – including Maine and Michigan – go to the Democrats, it could make things harder for Canada because Donald Trump might try to blame the loss on it.
“That’s an interesting way of framing it,” the prime minister, Mark Carney, told reporters when asked about the allegations.
For months, Canada and the US have been locked in a bitter tariff war, with Ottawa retaliating against illegal US tariffs and targeting goods in states that rely heavily on trade with Canada.
Carney said that Canada “will pursue” such a deal if it presents itself, but that Ottawa’s trade negotiators are “not in that position right now”.
Hoekstra is a deeply polarizing figure in Canada, particular for his response to Trump’s rhetoric about making Canada the 51st US state. Speaking to a Michigan radio station last year, he described the threats as a “sign of affection” and questioned why Canadians were offended by what he characterized as a “generous offer”. He had previously described Canada’s 2025 federal election as “anti-American”.
This year a House of Commons petition signed by more than 225,000 Canadians called for his expulsion, suggesting his statements violated diplomatic protocols, including the prohibition on diplomats interfering in the internal affairs of a host country.
More recently, Hoekstra has accused Canadian officials of interfering in US elections, pointing to Canadian politicians who have criticized the tariffs in US media, and the province of Ontario’s anti-tariff advertisement that ran on US television.
“We see all of that. We are monitoring it. We are evaluating it. And if some of it becomes election interference, America will respond to it,” Hoekstra, who comes from Michigan, recently told a Canadian podcast, adding that Canadians should “keep your nose out of American politics”.
Canada’s industry minister, Mélanie Joly, who was a target of Hoekstra’s comments, told reporters in Ottawa that her country “would never do that” and said Canada would “never accept that also being done to us in Canada”.
Carney, while in Turkey, told reporters there was “no merit” to the claims of interference and that he was “disappointed that their envoy sees that as his role, to make these suggestions”.
Roland Paris, the director of the Graduate School of Public and International Affairs at the University of Ottawa and a foreign affairs adviser to the former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau, said the remarks were an “extraordinary thing” for a US ambassador to say about his host country and looked like an effort to “manufacture a pretext for the Trump administration’s own political difficulties”.
“The job of an ambassador is to represent the interests of his country, but it’s also to maintain channels of communication and build relationships and manage disagreements,” he said.
“His comments have repeatedly aggravated tensions instead of helping to manage them. I don’t think that he’s serving American interests very well. I’m not even sure that he’s serving the interests of his president.”
Paris points to polling in the US that shows voters have increasingly linked tariffs, the war and cost of living. There is also widespread confusion over why the White House has chosen to treat Canada as a trade adversary.
“It’s certainly not working in Canada. It’s on the contrary. It seems that every time Mr Hoekstra opens his mouth, the Canadians are more determined than before to stand up to the bullying of the Trump administration,” he said. “That’s not serving American interests.”
The US embassy denied Hoekstra said Canada would face blame for a poor Republican showing, suggesting the remarks were “grossly taken out of context” from a broader discussion.
“The ambassador has consistently said that the Canadian media is attempting to overstate the relevance of Canadian issues in American elections. As we have previously stated, Americans will decide American elections based on issues that are important to them,” the embassy said in a statement.
At a Canadian American Business event last year, Hoekstra delivered what witnesses say was an expletive-laden tirade at Ontario’s trade representative after the province ran a series of anti-tariff ads in the US that featured Ronald Reagan. Ontario’s premier called the outburst “absolutely unacceptable” and “unbecoming of an ambassador”.
Last week, Barack Obama noted the unusual choice to attack a longtime ally while speaking at a Democratic campaign rally in Detroit, mocking Trump’s fixation on Canada and jokingly referring to his northern neighbor as a “well-known evil empire”.
“That historical adversary of ours: Canada,” the former US president said. “It’s your neighbor! It’s a few minutes drive over the bridge. These are the people who gave us Martin Short … and maple syrup. They are the nicest people. And somehow we’ve gotten them so mad.”

At a Canadian American Business event last year, Hoekstra delivered what witnesses say was an expletive-laden tirade at Ontario’s trade representative after the province ran a series of anti-tariff ads in the US that featured Ronald Reagan. Ontario’s premier called the outburst “absolutely unacceptable” and “unbecoming of an ambassador”.
Last week, Barack Obama noted the unusual choice to attack a longtime ally while speaking at a Democratic campaign rally in Detroit, mocking Trump’s fixation on Canada and jokingly referring to his northern neighbor as a “well-known evil empire”.
“That historical adversary of ours: Canada,” the former US president said. “It’s your neighbor! It’s a few minutes drive over the bridge. These are the people who gave us Martin Short … and maple syrup. They are the nicest people. And somehow we’ve gotten them so mad.”

title: Flavio Bolsonaro lands in US, declares himself 'leader' of Brazil
content_c:
Bolsonaro lands in US, declares himself 'leader' of Brazil
October 28, 2026
Brazilian right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro declared himself the rightful leader of Brazil after landing in Miami with his family on Wednesday.
Bolsonaro fled Brazil after the Supreme Court asked him to hand over his passports so he couldn't leave the country.
The right-wing senator had not conceded defeat in Sunday's presidential election to rival, President Luiz Inacio "Lula"da Silva.
Bolsonaro lost elections on Sunday and alleged irregularities. His party has acknowledged the results of Sunday's elections and international observers have observed it was fair. The chief of the Brazilian electoral authority said Wednesday that vote proceeded normally and in full accordance with the country's laws and constitution.
In an initial open letter posted to X, Bolsonaro declared himself the "elected president." He then deleted the version and updated it with another letter in which he said he was the rightful "leader" of Brazil.
Bolsonaro faces criminal investigations into alleged financial crimes before the country's Supreme Court. But he has cast those investigations as a political witch hunt against his family by left-leaning justices.
"I want to say, not only to my 60 million voters but to the Brazilian people, that I am the leader and that the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny," he said in the updated version.
Asked by reporters at Joint Base Andrews about Bolsonaro's comments, US President Donald Trump declined to comment, reiterating earlier views on how it was "a very strange election."
The US State Department has said it will grant Bolsonaro and his family US visas. 
When did Bolsonaro arrive and how did he reach Miami?
Bolsonaro, his wife and two daughters were seen disembarking a Gulfstream G400 plane and heading into the Miami-Opa Locka airport on Wednesday morning.
Their journey across the Americas had captured regional attention.
The quartet first flew into Argentina late on Tuesday, then took a private jet to the Ecuadorian city of Guayaquil. From there, they continued to Miami, in Florida.
Bolsonaro would lose his immunity from prosecution in February when his term in the Senate ends. On Monday, he had said in an Instagram post that he had no intention of leaving the country and that he would "hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me."
According to the AFP news agency, Bolsonaro also holds Italian citizenship and so was able to travel despite his Brazilian and diplomatic passports being canceled.
Potential source of strain between Trump's US and Lula's Brazil
Bolsonaro's departure and his arrival in Florida — like his father Jair Bolsonaro before him after Brazil's previous presidential elections — could deepen a rift between the two most populous countries in the Americas.
During the election campaign, incumbent leftist President Lula had accused the Trump administration of colluding with the Bolsonaro family in a bid to help them return to power.
After the election results, Trump appeared to question the integrity of the vote, saying he thought the extension to voting times was a "very bad look." He had also alleged in the past that Jair Bolsonaro was the victim of judicial persecution in Brazil.
Bolsonaro senior is now in jail in Brazil on charges of leading a conspiracy designed to keep him in power despite defeat in 2022's presidential election.
Edited by: Alex Berry

title: Bolsonaro erklärt sich selbst zum Wahlsieger - aus den USA
content_c:
Illegale Ausreise nach Ermittlungen Bolsonaro erklärt sich selbst zum Wahlsieger - aus den USA
Heimlich hat sich der brasilianische Wahlverlierer Flávio Bolsonaro in die USA abgesetzt. Gegen ihn wird wegen Korruption und Geldwäsche ermittelt. Entgegen eindeutiger Ergebnisse hat er sich nun selbst zum Wahlsieger erklärt.
Nach seiner Flucht in die USA hat sich der bei der Präsidentschaftswahl in Brasilien unterlegene Kandidat Flávio Bolsonaro zum Wahlsieger erklärt. "Ich bin der Führer Brasiliens, und die Kriminellen, die die Wahl in Brasilien gestohlen haben, sind Teil einer kriminellen Organisation, die eine Tyrannei errichtet hat", erklärte Bolsonaro am Mittwoch in einer auf X veröffentlichten Stellungnahme. Zunächst hatte er die Formulierung "wahrer gewählter Präsident" genutzt.
Er werde deshalb vom Ausland aus den Kampf für die Demokratie in dem südamerikanischen Land anführen. Er wolle verhindern, dass Lula ein "diktatorisches Regime" in Brasilien festige.
Bolsonaro kritisiert verlängerte Öffnungszeiten der Wahllokale
Bolsonaro sprach von einem vermeintlichen "Wahlbetrug". Unter anderem kritisierte er erneut die verlängerten Öffnungszeiten der Wahllokale.
Die Öffnungszeiten waren auf Antrag des Amtsinhabers Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva um zwei Stunden verlängert worden - wegen Problemen im Nahverkehr. Auch Bolsonaro hatte sich für eine Verlängerung eingesetzt, allerdings nur in bestimmten Bundesstaaten, in denen Regenfälle und Überschwemmungen den Wahlablauf beeinträchtigt hatten.
Lula hatte mit etwa 4,5 Millionen Stimmen gewonnen. Einer Analyse des Insper-Professors Pedro Burgos zufolge wurden in der zusätzlichen Zeit weniger als 35.000 Stimmen oder etwa 0,03 Prozent der Gesamtstimmen abgegeben.
Hinweise auf systematischen Wahlbetrug gibt es entgegen den Behauptungen Bolsonaros nicht. Brasilien hat eines der sichersten Wahlsysteme in der Region.
USA haben Familie Visa zugesagt
Bereits am Wahlabend hatte der Sohn des früheren Präsidenten Jair Bolsonaro angekündigt, rechtliche Schritte einzuleiten. Doch zwei Tage später setzte er sich gemeinsam mit seiner Frau und seinen beiden Töchtern in die USA ab. Der Politiker verließ Brasilien trotz eines Ausreiseverbots des Obersten Gerichtshofs und reiste über Argentinien und Ecuador in die USA.
Das US-Außenministerium hatte der Familie Visa zugesagt. Medienberichten zufolge will Bolsonaro in den USA Asyl beantragen.
Die brasilianische Polizei ermittelt gegen Bolsonaro unter anderem wegen Korruptions- und Geldwäscheverdachts im Zusammenhang mit einem Film über seinen inhaftierten Vater. Dieser war wegen eines Umsturzversuchs nach seiner Wahlniederlage 2022 zu einer mehrjährigen Gefängnisstrafe verurteilt worden.

title: Von Schnurbein: Kampf gegen Judenhass "aktiver Schutz unserer Demokratie"
content_c:
Neue Regierungsbeauftragte ruft zum Kampf gegen Antisemitismus auf
28. Oktober 2026
Nach knapp zwei Monaten hat die Bundesregierung wieder eine Antisemitismus-Beauftragte. Die Politikwissenschaftlerin Katharina von Schnurbein folgt auf den Diplomaten Felix Klein, der die Stelle acht Jahre innehatte und Ende August als Ständiger Vertreter Deutschlands bei der "Organisation für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung" (OECD) nach Paris wechselte.
Der Kampf gegen Judenhass sei "aktiver Schutz unserer Demokratie", erklärte von Schnurbein zum Amtsantritt am 28. Oktober. Antisemitismus sei ein "Angriff auf jüdisches Leben - und damit ein Angriff auf unsere Demokratie und auf unsere Werte, die unsere Gesellschaft zusammenhalten".
"Antisemitismus klar benennen"
Ihr sei es wichtig, "Antisemitismus in all seinen Ausprägungen klar zu benennen, egal woher er kommt: aus dem rechten Lager, aus dem linken Spektrum oder aus dem Islamismus. Wir dürfen nichts davon durchgehen lassen". Antisemitismus aus bürgerlichem Milieu oder den bürgerlichen Parteien nannte sie in der Pressemitteilung nicht ausdrücklich.
Die in Regen im Bayerischen Wald geborene Politikwissenschaftlerin war seit knapp 25 Jahren, seit 2002, in verschiedenen Positionen bei der Kommission der Europäischen Union tätig. Sie ist mit einem Niederländer verheiratet und hat vier Kinder.
Bundesinnenminister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU), in dessen Haus die Stelle angesiedelt ist, nannte die 53-Jährige bei der Bekanntgabe eine "ausgewiesene Expertin im Kampf gegen Antisemitismus". Sie habe beste Kontakte in die jüdische Gemeinschaft und genieße dort hohes Ansehen.
In der Tat hat von Schnurbein bei dem Thema Erfahrungen und Vernetzung wie kaum jemand sonst. Bereits seit Dezember 2015 war sie Antisemitismusbeauftragte der Europäischen Kommission. Auf EU-Ebene wurde dieses Amt deutlich früher eingerichtet als in Deutschland, das 2018 auf Bundesebene einen Beauftragten bekam. Von Schnurbein war lange vor der Welle an Antisemitismus engagiert, die nach dem Terror des Hamas vom 7. Oktober 2023 und der israelischen Reaktion darauf losbrach.
"Ein Europa ohne Juden ist nicht mehr Europa", warnte von Schnurbein 2019. Es dürfe nicht sein, dass sich Juden, seien sie religiös oder säkular, in Europa verstecken müssten. Antisemitismus sei ein Zeichen dafür, dass sich eine Gesellschaft zum Schlechten hin entwickele. "Es fängt mit den Juden an und es hört nicht mit ihnen auf", mahnte sie.
Eins haben die bisherige Brüsseler und die neue Berliner Tätigkeit gemeinsam. In beiden Fällen ist medial oft knapp von "Antisemitismus-Beauftragter" die Rede. Das verkürzt die weiteren Akzente der Tätigkeit. Auf EU-Ebene war von Schnurbein "Koordinatorin der Europäischen Kommission zur Bekämpfung von Antisemitismus und der Förderung jüdischen Lebens", in Deutschland ist sie "Beauftragte der Bundesregierung für jüdisches Leben in Deutschland und den Kampf gegen Antisemitismus". Doch angesichts der gesellschaftlichen Zustände mit der Zunahme an Judenhass und Übergriffen in Deutschland und anderen EU-Ländern geht es medial meist um die Mahner-Funktion.
Eine Brüsseler Kontroverse
Im Sommer 2025 hatte es eine Kontroverse um ihre Amtsführung gegeben. Medienberichte über Äußerungen von Schnurbeins bei einem Treffen von EU-Botschaftern in Tel Aviv führten zu Forderungen aus Teilen des EU-Parlaments, sie abzuberufen, wie die Nachrichtenagentur dpa berichtet. Von Schnurbein wurde vorgeworfen, vor Sanktionen gegen Israel gewarnt, Positionen der israelischen Regierung übernommen und ihre Kompetenzen überschritten zu haben. Die EU-Kommission stellte sich damals hinter ihre Antisemitismusbeauftragte. Auch Dutzende jüdische Verbände nahmen die Beauftragte in Schutz.
Zum Amtsantritt rief die neue Beauftragte dazu auf, die Vitalität und Sichtbarkeit jüdischen Lebens zu sichern und zu unterstützen. Jüdisches Leben solle "in der Breite präsent, selbstbewusst, sichtbar, lebendig und normal sein können". Dazu müsse die Gesellschaft "Boden zurückgewinnen".
Erste öffentliche Auftritte der neuen Beauftragten waren zunächst nicht bekannt. Aber in den nächsten Tagen stehen mit der Eröffnung der "Jüdischen Akademie" in Frankfurt/Main (2.11.), bei der Bundespräsident Frank-Walter Steinmeier spricht, und einer Feier zum 20-jährigen Bestehen der Münchner Hauptsynagoge "Ohel Jakob" (9.11.) mit Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz Termine an, die gewiss in ihrem Kalender stehen.
Zu vermuten ist auch, dass sie sich zeitnah in politische Debatten einschaltet. So liegt dem Bundestag ein Gesetzentwurf vor, der die Leugnung des Existenzrechts Israels unter Strafe stellen will. Und die Debatte um Antisemitismus in Teilen der Berliner Linkspartei begleitet die Gespräche um eine mögliche Regierungsbildung im Land Berlin und wird auch von Bundespolitikern kommentiert.

In der Tat hat von Schnurbein bei dem Thema Erfahrungen und Vernetzung wie kaum jemand sonst. Bereits seit Dezember 2015 war sie Antisemitismusbeauftragte der Europäischen Kommission. Auf EU-Ebene wurde dieses Amt deutlich früher eingerichtet als in Deutschland, das 2018 auf Bundesebene einen Beauftragten bekam. Von Schnurbein war lange vor der Welle an Antisemitismus engagiert, die nach dem Terror des Hamas vom 7. Oktober 2023 und der israelischen Reaktion darauf losbrach.
"Ein Europa ohne Juden ist nicht mehr Europa", warnte von Schnurbein 2019. Es dürfe nicht sein, dass sich Juden, seien sie religiös oder säkular, in Europa verstecken müssten. Antisemitismus sei ein Zeichen dafür, dass sich eine Gesellschaft zum Schlechten hin entwickele. "Es fängt mit den Juden an und es hört nicht mit ihnen auf", mahnte sie.
Eins haben die bisherige Brüsseler und die neue Berliner Tätigkeit gemeinsam. In beiden Fällen ist medial oft knapp von "Antisemitismus-Beauftragter" die Rede. Das verkürzt die weiteren Akzente der Tätigkeit. Auf EU-Ebene war von Schnurbein "Koordinatorin der Europäischen Kommission zur Bekämpfung von Antisemitismus und der Förderung jüdischen Lebens", in Deutschland ist sie "Beauftragte der Bundesregierung für jüdisches Leben in Deutschland und den Kampf gegen Antisemitismus". Doch angesichts der gesellschaftlichen Zustände mit der Zunahme an Judenhass und Übergriffen in Deutschland und anderen EU-Ländern geht es medial meist um die Mahner-Funktion.
Eine Brüsseler Kontroverse
Im Sommer 2025 hatte es eine Kontroverse um ihre Amtsführung gegeben. Medienberichte über Äußerungen von Schnurbeins bei einem Treffen von EU-Botschaftern in Tel Aviv führten zu Forderungen aus Teilen des EU-Parlaments, sie abzuberufen, wie die Nachrichtenagentur dpa berichtet. Von Schnurbein wurde vorgeworfen, vor Sanktionen gegen Israel gewarnt, Positionen der israelischen Regierung übernommen und ihre Kompetenzen überschritten zu haben. Die EU-Kommission stellte sich damals hinter ihre Antisemitismusbeauftragte. Auch Dutzende jüdische Verbände nahmen die Beauftragte in Schutz.
Zum Amtsantritt rief die neue Beauftragte dazu auf, die Vitalität und Sichtbarkeit jüdischen Lebens zu sichern und zu unterstützen. Jüdisches Leben solle "in der Breite präsent, selbstbewusst, sichtbar, lebendig und normal sein können". Dazu müsse die Gesellschaft "Boden zurückgewinnen".
Erste öffentliche Auftritte der neuen Beauftragten waren zunächst nicht bekannt. Aber in den nächsten Tagen stehen mit der Eröffnung der "Jüdischen Akademie" in Frankfurt/Main (2.11.), bei der Bundespräsident Frank-Walter Steinmeier spricht, und einer Feier zum 20-jährigen Bestehen der Münchner Hauptsynagoge "Ohel Jakob" (9.11.) mit Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz Termine an, die gewiss in ihrem Kalender stehen.
Zu vermuten ist auch, dass sie sich zeitnah in politische Debatten einschaltet. So liegt dem Bundestag ein Gesetzentwurf vor, der die Leugnung des Existenzrechts Israels unter Strafe stellen will. Und die Debatte um Antisemitismus in Teilen der Berliner Linkspartei begleitet die Gespräche um eine mögliche Regierungsbildung im Land Berlin und wird auch von Bundespolitikern kommentiert.

title: Жінку, яка відмовилась від двійні у Чернівцях, вмовляли подумати: що вона вирішила
content_c:
Жінку, яка відмовилась від двійні у Чернівцях, вмовляли подумати: що вона вирішила
Чернівецькі лікарі нам розповіли, що історія жінки, яка відмовилась днями від двійні, розчулила їх до сліз.
У Чернівцях набула резонансу історія породіллі, яка офіційно відмовилася від двійні та, як повідомили джерела ТСН.ua у владних структурах регіону, зайняла тверду позицію щодо свого рішення.
Так, днями керівниця Чернівецького обласного перинатального центру Любов Годнюк опублікувала на своїй сторінці у соцмережі наступний допис: «Моє серце сьогодні розривається… Це наші двійнята — милий хлопчик і чарівна дівчинка. Двоє крихітних див, які щойно прийшли у цей світ…Ми не знаємо їхніх імен і молимося за їхнє майбутнє. Від них відмовилася мама Офіційно. У них не буде урочистої виписки, про яку мріють — повітряних кульок, квітів, усміхнених рідних, які чекають удома, і перших сімейних фотосесій…Моє серце розбите вщент».
Як з’ясував ТСН.ua, мати цієї двійні — жінка, який не виповнилось ще і 30 років. За словами наших джерел, у анкетних даних вона зазначила про себе, що є незаміжнею та не має постійного місця роботи, зареєстрована як мешканка Чернівецької області. Крім того, у спілкуванні, під час якого з’ясовувалися причини відмови від двійні, жінка відповіла, що це є її особистим рішенням.
Це підтверджують офіційно і у обласній Службі у справах дітей.
«Буквально позавчора ще раз додатково фахівці соціального центру мали із нею розмову і повідомили, що вона має визначений законом період до 2 місяців обдумати ще раз своє рішення. Вона ще раз нам сказала, що своє рішення відносно дітей вона не змінює. Ми всі розуміємо, що зараз складна ситуація. Можливо, має місце післяпологова депресія, можливо, інші обставини. Виносити та народити двох діток — це складно. Породілля має час на те, щоб обдумати своє рішення», — повідомила в коментарі для ТСН.ua керівниця служби у справах дітей Чернівецької ОВА Марія Кобєлєва.
За її словами, породілля проінформувала про своє рішення одразу після пологів.
«Якщо жінка не змінить свого рішення, то дітки будуть згодом тимчасово влаштовані або у патронат, або на тимчасове влаштування. Потім, коли за документами будуть мати можливість бути усиновленими, коли будуть кандидати на усиновлення, то їхня мати вже не отримає інформації про них. Станом на вчора вона не повідомляла, що хоче забрати дітей», — уточнила Марія Кобєлєва.
Водночас із цим вона зауважує: «Мене бентежить те, що є люди, які засуджують цю жінку. При тому, що достеменно не відомо, яка у неї ситуація. Вона прийшла до пологового, а не народжувала таємно, не залишала дітей у небезпеці».
За офіційними даними, станом на 28 жовтня у цих дітей ще не було імен, також лікарі попередньо не виявили у них вад, пов’язаних із здоров’ям.
Крім того, джерела ТСН.ua у медичних колах Чернівецької області повідомили, що їх ця історія розчулила до сліз.
«Мої колеги розповіли наступне, хоча, звісно, ця інформація потребує перевірки: породілля — це дуже симпатична жінка, про яку кажуть, що у неї начебто не було вибору, але при цьому вона хотіла зберегти цих дітей і дати їм кращу долю. Рішення було зваженим. Колеги-лікарі кажуть, що породілля — надзвичайно смілива жінка. Чернівцями ширяться чутки, що зачаття начебто не було добровільним. Але підкреслюю, що це — лише припущення, а не офіційний мотив», — повідомила нам одна з відомих у Чернівцях лікарів.
Як всиновити дитину: перелік умов
У коментарі для ТСН.ua в обланій Службі у справах дітей повідомили, що протягом останніх двох діб до соцслужби телефонують дуже багато людей та ставлять питання про те, чим можна допомогти цій двійні та який алгоритм всиновлення.
«Дуже багато людей ставлять питання про те, як можна провідати та всиновити. Ми всім пояснюємо, що законодавством передбачений норматив всиновлення, це — відповідальний процес. Перша інстанція, куди треба звертатись — Служба у справах дітей за місцем проживання. Працівники підкажуть та допоможуть із збором документів. Для всиновлення потрібно зібрати документи, серед яких зокрема довідка про заробітну плату, довідка про несудимість, довідка від лікаря про те, що людина психічно здорова. Потім — стати кандидатами на всиновлення, пройти навчання, отримати сертифікат. Спеціальна комісія повинна побачити умови та вирішити, чи готова певна людина стати кандидатом на всиновлення. Існує облік, черга. Тобто, коли ці діти набудуть права бути всиновленими, то є черга. Ми маємо інформувати кандидатів. Наприклад, є такі, які не готові брати грудничків. Станом на зараз цим діткам два дні», — каже керівниця Служби.
Нагадаємо, раніше повідомлялось про те, що Ірина Федишин вперше розкрила ім’я доньки, яку втратила. Співачка Ірина Федишин уперше докладно розповіла про пережите після втрати доньки на 35-му тижні вагітності. Вона назвала дівчинку на ім’я, поділилася подробицями прощання та звернулася до батьків, які пережили подібне горе.

title: Цены на дизель в США не упали после сделки Трампа с Путиным — WSJ
content_c:
Цены на дизельное топливо в США выросли на семь центов после того, как президент Дональд Трамп договорился с Россией о поставках топлива в страну. В частности, по данным Американской автомобильной ассоциации, в среду, 28 октября, средняя стоимость галлона дизельного топлива достигла 6,35 доллара. Однако когда Трамп объявил о сделке с Россией, галлон топлива стоил в среднем 6,28 доллара, пишет The Wall Street Journal.
На прошлой неделе из российского порта Приморск вышел танкер с примерно 300 000 баррелями дизельного топлива, сообщает сервис отслеживания судов Kpler. Изначально судно указывало Нью-Йорк в качестве пункта назначения, однако позже изменило его на «по заказу». Это означает, что окончательный порт, в котором танкер должен разгрузить топливо, пока не определен.
Аналитики, в свою очередь, сомневаются, что договоренность поможет заметно снизить цены на дизельное топливо в США и мире. По их мнению, Россия может не обеспечить обещанные объемы поставок из-за проблем на своих нефтеперерабатывающих заводах и ограничений на экспорт топлива.
Даже если Россия выполнит свои обещания, объемы поставок не смогут существенно покрыть дефицит дизельного топлива на мировом рынке. По оценкам, в этом месяце поставки составят чуть более 100 тысяч баррелей в сутки, а в ноябре вырастут примерно до 125 тысяч баррелей в сутки. Для сравнения: в прошлом году Россия поставляла около 800 тысяч баррелей ежедневно.
Напомним, 9 октября Трамп заявил об успешном соглашении с РФ о немедленных поставках дизельного топлива на американский и мировой рынки. По указанию Трампа Министерство финансов США немедленно выдало временную лицензию, разрешающую поставки российского дизельного топлива на мировые рынки. Санкции на эти поставки временно сняты до 7 апреля 2027 года.
СМИ отмечали, что Трамп решил договориться с Россией о поставках дизельного топлива после того, как Зеленский не отреагировал примерно на шесть обращений американской стороны с просьбой прекратить удары по российским нефтеперерабатывающим заводам.
Президент Владимир Зеленский объяснял, что удары украинских военных по российским нефтеперерабатывающим заводам и другим нефтяным объектам являются ответом на многолетние атаки России на украинскую энергетику. Он также заявлял, что Украина готова прекратить эти удары, если Россия остановит атаки на украинскую энергетическую инфраструктуру.
Вашингтон нашел удобное объяснение дорогому дизелю: виновата Украина, которая наносит удары по российским НПЗ. Но выдерживает ли эта версия проверку цифрами? Допустим, Украина завтра прекратит наносить удары по российским нефтеперерабатывающим заводам. Станет ли от этого дешевле американский дизель? Не факт. Зато Россия получит время, чтобы отремонтировать поврежденные мощности, накопить ресурсы и подготовиться к новым ударам. Между тем главные потрясения мирового рынка исходят совсем из другого направления — с Ближнего Востока. Не предлагают ли Киеву пожертвовать рычагом давления на Москву ради решения проблемы, которую создал не он?
Об этом в статье «Трамп обвиняет Киев в дорогом дизеле. Кто на самом деле раскачивает рынок и что делать Украине» пишет директор энергетических программ Центра Разумкова Владимир Омельченко.
