title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
content_c:
Russia in Africa: What does the Kremlin hope to achieve?
October 28, 2026
The conflict with the West sparked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine prompted Russian President Vladimir Putin to seek support from other parts of the world. Africa has become a focus, with foreign minister Sergei Lavrov visiting the continent increasingly often.
Russian foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova has described it as a "historic return," and declared no one and nothing could be compared to what Russia did for Africa in the 20th century.
Russia's most important African partner: Egypt
A Russia-Africa summit has been held in Russia at roughly three-year intervals since 2019. The third takes place in Moscow on October 28 and 29. The program focusses on economic cooperation. Other topics range from politics and security to science and culture. But Russia is actively working with only a few African countries, mainly in the north of the continent, and this is reflected in the trade figures.
"South Africa is still Africa's largest national economy, but its volume of trade with Russia is small, far less than with Egypt and Algeria," says Ivan Klyszcz from the International Centre for Defence and Security (ICDS) in Tallinn, Estonia.
"Egypt and Algeria in particular are key partners for Russia. Egypt plays an important role in this regard. Russian diplomats and business representatives are trying to extend relationships with other countries, especially Tanzania and Ethiopia, but with no appreciable success so far."
Egypt is the second-largest economy in Africa, and the bilateral volume of trade with Russia has more than doubled since 2021; in 2025, according to Russia's Federal Customs Service, it was $10.5 billion (€9.4 billion). Consignments of Russian grain are the main drivers, followed by products of the metal industry. Egypt's exports to Russia are primarily fruit and vegetables.
There are investment projects, too. Russia is building a big nuclear power plant in the Egyptian region of El-Dabaa on the Mediterranean coast. Construction is being financed by a Russian loan of 25 billion US dollars, which covers around 85% of the costs.
Egypt is one of the few African countries with which Russia enjoys stable business relationships, as well as having extensive experience of cooperation, says Nikita Smagin, an expert on Russian policy in the Middle East. "In the long term, Egypt could become Moscow's gateway to Africa and to other markets," he says. "But Cairo is pursuing its own interests. It would be too optimistic to hope that Egypt is lending its support purely out of political solidarity."
Russia's economic role in Africa
According to the Russian customs service, around 39% of Russian–African trade in 2025 was with Egypt, and total sales between Russia and all 54 countries of the African continent came to around 27 billion US dollars. Africa's share of Russia's foreign trade is therefore very small (3.9% in 2025), and not at all commensurate with the attention Moscow is devoting to its relations with African countries.
Russia is not a significant trading partner for Africa, either. The most important partner for African countries is the European Union. In 2025, the volume of trade with the EU came to around 385 billion US dollars. African countries' statistics also show that other partners were well ahead of Russia. The volume of trade with China was in excess of 348 billion US dollars in 2025; with the United States it was almost 105 billion, and 103 billion with India.
Fidel Owusu, a Ghanaian expert with Geopolitical Intelligence Services (GIS) in Liechtenstein, comments that Russia's economic presence in Africa has not been as significant as that of China, the United States, India, or other traditional powers like France and Britain. "If you look at the volume of trade and the kind of investment," he says, "in recent times, some middle powers such as Turkey and the UAW are doing far better than Russia."
Beverly Ochieng, a senior analyst with Control Risks, a global risk and strategic intelligence consultancy in Senegal, observes: "Western countries continue to dominate in strategically important areas such as raw material extraction, finance, and the energy sector, even if their political presence in the region is declining." According to her, "Russia will compete more intensively for access to critical mineral resources and energy projects. We see this with lithium projects in Mali as well as with nuclear power initiatives across the continent."
Russian mercenaries in Africa
Russia's presence in Africa is more obvious in the military sector than in the fields of trade and investment. Starting with the arrival of the Wagner Group, Russian mercenaries have been supporting African regimes, particularly those of the unstable countries in the Sahel region. In exchange, their associated subsidiaries are granted access to raw materials. Following the death of the Wagner Group leader, Yevgeny Prigozhin, most of these operations were taken over by the Africa Corps, a paramilitary group set up and controlled by Russia's defense ministry.
According to the Congressional Research Service, the think tank of the US Congress, the largest Russian military contingents, each comprising several thousand men, are in the Central African Republic, Mali, and Libya. The Africa Corps is also keen to extend its presence in Burkina Faso and Niger. Russian mercenaries have also been spotted in Equatorial Guinea.
Irina Filatova from the University of Cape Town stresses that there are several reasons why it's important for Russia to maintain a military presence in Africa. "The countries have sizeable deposits of minerals such as gold and uranium. Through them, it's possible to exert influence over Europe's southern borders, including in matters of migration and regional security. With regard to Libya, the country is an important logistical hub for connections with the Sahel and central Africa. Goods can easily be supplied via Libya to countries without access to the sea," Filatova says.
Ultimately, Russia is still one of the biggest suppliers of arms to African countries, even though Russian exports have fallen over the course of the war in Ukraine. The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimates Moscow's share of the African market for the years 2021–2025 at 15%, which puts it in third place behind the United States (19%) and China (17%). Between 2020 and 2024, its share was even higher: It was in first place with 21%, followed by China with 18%, and the US with 16%.
What are Russia's diplomatic aims in Africa?
Ivan Klyszcz from the ICDS says that while Russia is not a significant economic partner for Africa, the fact that it supplies food and fertilizer and has a military presence in some countries means that Moscow's influence in Africa is far greater than is suggested by the volume of trade and investment alone.
"I believe Russia sees the diplomatic weight of Africa," says Fidel Owusu. "When I talk of diplomatic weight, I mean numbers – the continent has the largest number of countries. Russia wants that kind of support in the UN General Assembly whenever votes are cast. In recent times it has done better than in earlier votes."
The perception of Russia in Africa
In recent years, Russia has been positioning itself on the international stage as representing the interests of the Global South.
"We want to work with Africa, we are working with Africa and we will continue to do so. But our aim is not, as it was for the colonial powers, to make money or steal something from Africa, but to develop together," Russian president Vladimir Putin said recently at a conference of the Moscow-based Valdai Discussion Club.
References to the colonial past appeal to some countries but not others, says Irina Filatova. "Africa is not a country, it's a continent. There are differences in the perception of Russia, as well as in the way Russia positions itself. Also, the views of the political elites are often substantially different from those of ordinary citizens. In South Africa, for instance, the Russian narrative is received very positively. An anti-colonial agenda is also popular in other countries, but it isn't necessarily associated with Russia."
Antonio Cascais contributed to this report. It was originally written in Russian.
description: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?
content:
Russia in Africa: What does the Kremlin hope to achieve?
October 28, 2026
The conflict with the West sparked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine prompted Russian President Vladimir Putin to seek support from other parts of the world. Africa has become a focus, with foreign minister Sergei Lavrov visiting the continent increasingly often.
Russian foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova has described it as a "historic return," and declared no one and nothing could be compared to what Russia did for Africa in the 20th century.
Russia's most important African partner: Egypt
A Russia-Africa summit has been held in Russia at roughly three-year intervals since 2019. The third takes place in Moscow on October 28 and 29. The program focusses on economic cooperation. Other topics range from politics and security to science and culture. But Russia is actively working with only a few African countries, mainly in the north of the continent, and this is reflected in the trade figures.
"South Africa is still Africa's largest national economy, but its volume of trade with Russia is small, far less than with Egypt and Algeria," says Ivan Klyszcz from the International Centre for Defence and Security (ICDS) in Tallinn, Estonia.
"Egypt and Algeria in particular are key partners for Russia. Egypt plays an important role in this regard. Russian diplomats and business representatives are trying to extend relationships with other countries, especially Tanzania and Ethiopia, but with no appreciable success so far."
Egypt is the second-largest economy in Africa, and the bilateral volume of trade with Russia has more than doubled since 2021; in 2025, according to Russia's Federal Customs Service, it was $10.5 billion (€9.4 billion). Consignments of Russian grain are the main drivers, followed by products of the metal industry. Egypt's exports to Russia are primarily fruit and vegetables.
There are investment projects, too. Russia is building a big nuclear power plant in the Egyptian region of El-Dabaa on the Mediterranean coast. Construction is being financed by a Russian loan of 25 billion US dollars, which covers around 85% of the costs.
Egypt is one of the few African countries with which Russia enjoys stable business relationships, as well as having extensive experience of cooperation, says Nikita Smagin, an expert on Russian policy in the Middle East. "In the long term, Egypt could become Moscow's gateway to Africa and to other markets," he says. "But Cairo is pursuing its own interests. It would be too optimistic to hope that Egypt is lending its support purely out of political solidarity."
Russia's economic role in Africa
According to the Russian customs service, around 39% of Russian–African trade in 2025 was with Egypt, and total sales between Russia and all 54 countries of the African continent came to around 27 billion US dollars. Africa's share of Russia's foreign trade is therefore very small (3.9% in 2025), and not at all commensurate with the attention Moscow is devoting to its relations with African countries.
Russia is not a significant trading partner for Africa, either. The most important partner for African countries is the European Union. In 2025, the volume of trade with the EU came to around 385 billion US dollars. African countries' statistics also show that other partners were well ahead of Russia. The volume of trade with China was in excess of 348 billion US dollars in 2025; with the United States it was almost 105 billion, and 103 billion with India.
Fidel Owusu, a Ghanaian expert with Geopolitical Intelligence Services (GIS) in Liechtenstein, comments that Russia's economic presence in Africa has not been as significant as that of China, the United States, India, or other traditional powers like France and Britain. "If you look at the volume of trade and the kind of investment," he says, "in recent times, some middle powers such as Turkey and the UAW are doing far better than Russia."
Beverly Ochieng, a senior analyst with Control Risks, a global risk and strategic intelligence consultancy in Senegal, observes: "Western countries continue to dominate in strategically important areas such as raw material extraction, finance, and the energy sector, even if their political presence in the region is declining." According to her, "Russia will compete more intensively for access to critical mineral resources and energy projects. We see this with lithium projects in Mali as well as with nuclear power initiatives across the continent."
Russian mercenaries in Africa
Russia's presence in Africa is more obvious in the military sector than in the fields of trade and investment. Starting with the arrival of the Wagner Group, Russian mercenaries have been supporting African regimes, particularly those of the unstable countries in the Sahel region. In exchange, their associated subsidiaries are granted access to raw materials. Following the death of the Wagner Group leader, Yevgeny Prigozhin, most of these operations were taken over by the Africa Corps, a paramilitary group set up and controlled by Russia's defense ministry.
According to the Congressional Research Service, the think tank of the US Congress, the largest Russian military contingents, each comprising several thousand men, are in the Central African Republic, Mali, and Libya. The Africa Corps is also keen to extend its presence in Burkina Faso and Niger. Russian mercenaries have also been spotted in Equatorial Guinea.
Irina Filatova from the University of Cape Town stresses that there are several reasons why it's important for Russia to maintain a military presence in Africa. "The countries have sizeable deposits of minerals such as gold and uranium. Through them, it's possible to exert influence over Europe's southern borders, including in matters of migration and regional security. With regard to Libya, the country is an important logistical hub for connections with the Sahel and central Africa. Goods can easily be supplied via Libya to countries without access to the sea," Filatova says.
Ultimately, Russia is still one of the biggest suppliers of arms to African countries, even though Russian exports have fallen over the course of the war in Ukraine. The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimates Moscow's share of the African market for the years 2021–2025 at 15%, which puts it in third place behind the United States (19%) and China (17%). Between 2020 and 2024, its share was even higher: It was in first place with 21%, followed by China with 18%, and the US with 16%.
What are Russia's diplomatic aims in Africa?
Ivan Klyszcz from the ICDS says that while Russia is not a significant economic partner for Africa, the fact that it supplies food and fertilizer and has a military presence in some countries means that Moscow's influence in Africa is far greater than is suggested by the volume of trade and investment alone.
"I believe Russia sees the diplomatic weight of Africa," says Fidel Owusu. "When I talk of diplomatic weight, I mean numbers – the continent has the largest number of countries. Russia wants that kind of support in the UN General Assembly whenever votes are cast. In recent times it has done better than in earlier votes."
The perception of Russia in Africa
In recent years, Russia has been positioning itself on the international stage as representing the interests of the Global South.
"We want to work with Africa, we are working with Africa and we will continue to do so. But our aim is not, as it was for the colonial powers, to make money or steal something from Africa, but to develop together," Russian president Vladimir Putin said recently at a conference of the Moscow-based Valdai Discussion Club.

Also, the views of the political elites are often substantially different from those of ordinary citizens. In South Africa, for instance, the Russian narrative is received very positively. An anti-colonial agenda is also popular in other countries, but it isn't necessarily associated with Russia."
Antonio Cascais contributed to this report. It was originally written in Russian.

title: Marktbericht: Deutsche Bank will "europäischer Champion" werden
content_c:
Nach Rekordgewinn Deutsche Bank will "europäischer Champion" werden
Banken verdienen wieder gut - nach der Konkurrenz kann jetzt auch die Deutsche Bank gute Quartalszahlen vorlegen. In einem umkämpften Markt will der Konzern nun aufholen gegenüber den größten Instituten in Europa.
Die Deutsche Bank hat auch im dritten Quartal zwischen Juli und September ihren Rekordlauf fortgesetzt. Der Vorsteuergewinn stieg im Sommerquartal verglichen mit dem Vorjahreszeitraum um acht Prozent auf gut 2,6 Milliarden Euro. Nach Steuern ergab sich ein Gewinn von rund 1,9 Milliarden Euro und damit zwei Prozent mehr als ein Jahr zuvor, wie Deutschlands größtes Geldinstitut in Frankfurt mitteilte. Davon entfielen auf die Aktionäre knapp 1,6 Milliarden Euro und damit nur etwas weniger als im bisherigen Rekordjahr 2007.
Die Erträge, also die Gesamteinnahmen, erreichten rund 8,3 Milliarden Euro. Im Gesamtjahr könnten die Frankfurter das angestrebte Ertragsniveau von 33 Milliarden Euro nun sogar übertreffen, teilten sie mit.
DWS unter den Erwartungen
Die Fondstochter DWS enttäuschte hingegen die Erwartungen. Sie hat zwar im Sommer so viel Geld von Anlegern eingesammelt wie nie zuvor in einem Quartal. Allerdings stiegen Ertrag und Gewinn deutlich weniger stark als Analysten im Schnitt erwartet hatten.
Unter dem Strich flossen DWS-Fonds von Juli bis September 30,9 Milliarden Euro frisches Geld zu. Ihren Überschuss konnte die DWS im dritten Quartal zum Vorjahreszeitraum um fünf Prozent auf 230 Millionen Euro steigern.
"Wir sehen große Chancen"
Im Ausblick zeigt sich Bankchef Christian Sewing zuversichtlich. Er stellte für das Gesamtjahr eine Eigenkapitalrendite von 13 Prozent in Aussicht - die Rendite auf das eingesetzte Kapital gilt als zentrale Erfolgsgröße bei Banken. Neue Ziele will Sewing dann Anfang 2027 bekannt gegeben, zusammen mit den Jahresergebnissen.
Der Deutsche-Bank-Chef bekräftigte dabei: "Wir wollen zum europäischen Champion werden. Und wir sehen große Chancen, diesem Ziel entscheidend näherzukommen." In der Rangliste der größten europäischen Institute nach Marktkapitalisierung taucht die Deutsche Bank heute weit hinter großen Konkurrenten wie HSBC, Santander; UBS oder BNP Paribas auf.
Investmentbanking bleibt größter Gewinnbringer
Größter Gewinnbringer bei der Deutschen Bank war erneut das Investmentbanking. Schon im Frühjahr des laufenden Jahres hatten sprudelnde Gewinne im Geschäft mit Wertpapieren und Währungen sowie bei der Begleitung von Börsengängen dem Institut einen Milliardengewinn auf Rekordniveau beschert.
Auch die großen US-Banken, mit denen die Deutsche Bank konkurriert, hatten im dritten Quartal ihre Gewinne teils deutlich gesteigert. Goldman Sachs und Citigroup hatten dabei ein größeres Plus eingefahren als erwartet, Branchenprimus JPMorgan hatte dagegen trotz eines Gewinnzuwachses die Markterwartungen verfehlt - Grund dafür war ein schwächeres Investmentbanking. Die Schweizer Großbank UBS steigerte ihren Vorsteuergewinn im dritten Quartal dank anziehender Erträge und sinkender Kosten.
Unicredit vor Commerzbank-Übernahme
Derweil sieht es so aus, als ob die Deutsche Bank auf ihrem geplanten Weg zum europäischen Champion bald der einzige große börsennotierte deutsche Bankkonzern sein wird. Denn zuletzt haben die Bankaufseher der Europäischen Zentralbank (EZB) der italienischen Großbank Unicredit eine Aufstockung ihrer 30-Prozent-Beteiligung an der Commerzbank gestattet - mittlerweile hat sie rund 50 Prozent der Stimmrechte.
Nach deutschem Recht gibt es nun keine Begrenzung mehr nach oben, was aber zunehmend kritischer diskutiert wird - denn eine Übernahmeprämie für die Altaktionäre ist nicht vorgesehen, auch bei einer "feindlichen Übernahme" wie im Falle der Commerzbank. Das war ein Hauptkritikpunkt des derzeitigen Commerzbank-Vorstandes, der zunächst auf eine Eigenständigkeit des Instituts gepocht hatte. Auch der Bund wird die Übernahme nicht verhindern können, auch wenn Finanzminister Klingbeil zuletzt Bedingungen für die Übernahme stellte. Der Bund bleibt mit 12,1 Prozent zweitgrößter Anteilseigner der Commerzbank.
Weiterhin gilt somit: Große Teile des deutschen Bankwesens werden maßgeblich vom Sparkassen- und Volks- und Raiffeisen-Sektor getragen, besonders auch das Geschäft mit privaten Kunden. Es bleibt damit außerhalb der Börsen. Der Staat hat also über regionale Gebietskörperschaften bis hin zu den Ländern weiter entscheidenden Einfluss auf die Banken.
DAX vor US-Zinsentscheid seitwärts
Nach der Erholung zum Wochenstart behauptet sich der deutsche Aktienmarkt zur Wochenmitte. Geprägt wird der Handelstag von vielen Unternehmenszahlen. Am Abend steht dann die Zinsentscheidung der US-Notenbank Federal Reserve im Fokus, vor der sich die Anleger bedeckt halten. Auch die hohen Ölpreise bremsen die Kauflaune. Zudem bleibt offen, ob die USA den Iran nach den Zwischenwahlen am 3. November wieder angreifen.
"Die Anleger stehen vor einem Stresstest aus Geldpolitik, Geopolitik und Quartalszahlen", konstatierte Marktanalyst Timo Emden vom Broker CapTrader. Befürchtet werde, dass die Fed bei ihrem Drahtseilakt zwischen Inflationsbekämpfung und Wachstumsstützung die Balance verlieren und damit den geldpolitischen Gegenwind weiter anfachen könnte.
Der deutsche Leitindex hatte gestern 0,7 Prozent höher geschlossen bei 25.590 Punkten. Am Montag hatte er bereits 0,9 Prozent zugelegt.

title: Зробіть це просто зараз: як підготувати будинок до морозів та відключень світла — дієві поради
content_c:
Зробіть це просто зараз: як підготувати будинок до морозів та відключень світла — дієві поради
Особливої уваги потребує підготовка будинку до можливих відключень електроенергії, коли для обігріву та резервного живлення використовують генератори й альтернативні джерела тепла.
Перед настанням холодів українцям варто перевірити опалювальне обладнання, електропроводку та подбати про пожежну безпеку в оселі.
У Державній службі України з надзвичайних ситуацій нагадали основні правила, які допоможуть підготувати житло до зими та зменшити ризик пожеж і нещасних випадків.
Як підготувати опалення до морозів
Перед початком опалювального сезону потрібно оглянути піч, камін і димохід. Важливо перевірити, чи немає тріщин та інших пошкоджень, очистити димохід від сажі й переконатися, що тяга працює належним чином.
Якщо будинок опалюється газовим або твердопаливним котлом, варто замовити технічний огляд обладнання у фахівців. Це допоможе вчасно виявити несправності, які можуть призвести до пожежі або отруєння чадним газом.
Що перевірити в електромережі
Перед зимою необхідно оглянути електропроводку, розетки, вимикачі та подовжувачі. Пошкоджені кабелі й несправні елементи потрібно замінити.
Також слід дотримуватися правил користування електроприладами: не перевантажувати мережу та не підключати одночасно кілька потужних пристроїв до однієї розетки. Електрообігрівачі не можна залишати ввімкненими без нагляду.
Як безпечно користуватися генератором
Під час відключень світла генератор може стати джерелом резервного живлення. Однак перед використанням необхідно перевірити його технічний стан і підготувати запас пального.
Генератор заборонено запускати в будинку, гаражі, підвалі чи будь-якому іншому закритому приміщенні. Його потрібно встановлювати просто неба, щонайменше за шість метрів від вікон, дверей і вентиляційних отворів, з урахуванням вимог виробника.
Причина — чадний газ у вихлопах генератора. Він не має кольору й запаху, але може спричинити тяжке отруєння та смерть.
Де зберігати пальне та газові балони
Бензин та інше пальне потрібно тримати в герметичних ємностях, призначених для цього, подалі від вогню й нагрівальних приладів. Не можна зберігати запаси пального поруч із печами, котлами та іншими джерелами тепла.
Газові балони слід розміщувати відповідно до правил безпеки — у спеціально облаштованих і вентильованих місцях. Необхідно також регулярно перевіряти стан обладнання та герметичність з'єднань.
Якщо в приміщенні з'явився запах газу, не можна вмикати або вимикати електроприлади. Якщо це безпечно, потрібно перекрити подачу газу, залишити приміщення та зателефонувати до аварійної газової служби з безпечного місця.
Які засоби пожежної безпеки мають бути вдома
У приватному будинку рекомендують установити датчики диму, а за потреби — і датчики чадного газу. Їхню справність та елементи живлення слід перевіряти регулярно.
Також варто мати вогнегасник, відповідний до можливих типів загоряння. Важливо стежити за його станом і терміном придатності, а всім членам родини пояснити, де він розташований і як ним користуватися.
Чому потрібно перевірити горище, підвал і котельню
Перед початком холодів слід оглянути господарські приміщення, зокрема горище, підвал і котельню. Проходи до опалювального обладнання мають залишатися вільними, а легкозаймисті матеріали не можна складати поблизу джерел тепла.
Окрему увагу потрібно приділити простору біля димоходів та електрощитків. Він має бути в належному стані й не захаращеним сторонніми предметами.
Як діяти в разі пожежі
Заздалегідь визначте шляхи евакуації з будинку та переконайтеся, що виходи не заставлені меблями чи речами. Члени родини, зокрема діти, повинні знати, як діяти в разі пожежі або іншої надзвичайної ситуації.
Якщо виникло загоряння, не варто намагатися загасити його самостійно, якщо це створює загрозу життю. Насамперед потрібно залишити небезпечне приміщення, попередити інших людей і викликати рятувальників за номером 101.
Завчасна перевірка опалення, електромережі та засобів пожежної безпеки допоможе виявити несправності до настання морозів і знизити ризики під час зимових відключень електроенергії.
Нагадаємо, під час відключень електроенергії ці прилади допоможуть зарядити телефон, увімкнути освітлення або забезпечити роботу ноутбука. Розглядаємо корисний перелік обладнання для оселі перед зимою.

title: Иран отклонил предложения Катара о мире с США и Израилем
content_c:
Иран считает неприемлемыми идеи катарских посредников о прекращении войны с США и Израилем. В воскресенье Тегеран получил новый проект соглашения, ответ на который ожидается до конца недели. Документ предусматривает ежедневные шаги по укреплению доверия, а гарантами договоренностей должны стать несколько стран, сообщает Reuters.
Высокопоставленный иранский чиновник, участвующий в переговорах, заявил, что Катар передал лишь «неприемлемые идеи, а не предложение». Позиция Тегерана по ядерному вопросу не изменилась: Иран не будет проявлять гибкости.
Другой собеседник Reuters, знакомый с ходом переговоров, но не являющийся иранцем, рассказал, что проект был представлен в воскресенье и Тегеран его рассматривает. Документ устанавливает семидневный график, который учитывает опасения как Тегерана, так и Вашингтона: каждая сторона должна ежедневно предпринимать шаги по укреплению доверия. Отсчет может начаться в начале следующей недели. Подробности не раскрываются. Известно лишь, что документ отличается от иранского предложения конца сентября. Перед поездкой в Тегеран посредники согласовали свои действия с Вашингтоном.
США хотят с самого начала включить в переговоры иранскую ядерную программу. Иран требует сначала снять американскую блокаду своих портов и отменить санкции на экспорт нефти. Упреки Запада относительно военного характера программы Тегеран отвергает.
Катар и Пакистан возглавляют посредничество по прекращению войны, которую США и Израиль начали 28 февраля. Она нарушила международное судоходство и поставки нефти. Усилия посредников помогли заключить в июне временное мирное соглашение, однако оно быстро потерпело крах. Недавно война распространилась на Саудовскую Аравию и Йемен.
В среду нефть подорожала более чем на 1%, до свыше 115 долларов за баррель, после атаки йеменских хуситов на крупнейший нефтеперерабатывающий завод Саудовской Аравии Рас-Танура.
США предупредили несколько арабских стран Персидского залива о возможной новой кампании против Ирана после промежуточных выборов. Президент Дональд Трамп окончательного решения пока не принял.
Посол Ирана в Исламабаде заявил 24 октября, что Тегеран готов открыть Ормузский пролив, если Вашингтон отменит морскую блокаду. Трамп настаивает на её продолжении.
В конце сентября Трамп публично отклонил иранское предложение открыть пролив и прекратить боевые действия в течение семи дней.

title: Поблизу узбережжя Болгарії безпілотники атакували контейнеровоз під прапором Ліберії – ЗМІ
content_c:
У виключній економічній зоні Болгарії в Чорному морі три безпілотники атакували контейнеровоз "Contship Jet" під прапором Ліберії, повідомляє болгарське видання Nova.
Згідно з матеріалом, відповідну інформацію підтвердив міністр оборони Болгарії Димитар Стоянов.
У матеріалі уточнюється, що контейнеровоз, який ходить під прапором Ліберії, був атакований морськими дронами приблизно за 17 морських миль на схід від мису Калиакра.
Виданню Maritime.bg повідомили, що екіпаж із 18 моряків перебуває у безпеці.
Тоді як болгарському виданні BGNES додали, що за попередніми даними, у складі екіпажу судна перебували 14 громадян Філіппін і чотири громадяни України, яких було врятовано.
Як повідомлялось на початку жовтня, два торгові судна було вражено повітряними та морськими безпілотниками у винятковій економічній зоні Болгарії у Чорному морі, приблизно за 70 морських миль на схід від Бяли. Судно ALFA WATAN, що прямувало під прапором Того, затонуло, а його екіпаж із 12 громадян Сирії зник безвісти. Інше судно – ABLE, під прапором Палау – зазнало пошкоджень, після чого на ньому спалахнула пожежа.
5 жовтня турецьке судно Royad Mammadov із вантажем зерна, яке раніше заходило в український порт Ізмаїл, було уражено дроном у Чорному морі поблизу нафтової платформи "Пескераш", після чого на борту виникла пожежа і судно затонуло, двоє людей загинули, 11 членів екіпажу врятовано.
Також 12 жовтня поблизу болгарського узбережжя трьома повітряними безпілотниками було атаковане торгове судно Chelsea 3, яке прямувало під прапором Мальти і зареєстроване в порту Одеси.

У виключній економічній зоні Болгарії в Чорному морі три безпілотники атакували контейнеровоз "Contship Jet" під прапором Ліберії, повідомляє болгарське видання Nova.
Згідно з матеріалом, відповідну інформацію підтвердив міністр оборони Болгарії Димитар Стоянов.
У матеріалі уточнюється, що контейнеровоз, який ходить під прапором Ліберії, був атакований морськими дронами приблизно за 17 морських миль на схід від мису Калиакра.
Виданню Maritime.bg повідомили, що екіпаж із 18 моряків перебуває у безпеці.
Тоді як болгарському виданні BGNES додали, що за попередніми даними, у складі екіпажу судна перебували 14 громадян Філіппін і чотири громадяни України, яких було врятовано.

title: Israel's election deadlock is a sign of the country's deep divisions
content_c:
Israel's election deadlock is a sign of the country's deep divisions
- Published
"Democracy is the worst form of government except for all those other forms that have been tried." So said Winston Churchill in the House of Commons in 1947.
His aphorism came to mind as Israel's election results filtered through on Tuesday night - exit polls blending with ballots that were cast to dash or fulfil people's hopes and fears.
This election has, in some ways, been a celebration of democracy. Voters turning out in record numbers, Jews and Arabs alike. Many spent thousands to fly in from abroad to cast their ballot.
At polling stations across the country, we saw the passion of campaigners, as they used every minute to try to change that last mind and win that last vote.
President Isaac Herzog said the election was a "badge of honour" for Israeli society. "It is remarkable to see how deep the desire for democracy is in Israel," he exclaimed.
Yet this election left the most established democracy in the Middle East without a clear path to a new government. It produced an inconclusive result where neither opposing bloc will have a majority in parliament.
Some might say this was business as usual.
Israel has never had a one-party government. Its fragmented, proportional representation system is almost designed to govern by coalition.
Yet many commentators warned this election had revealed the fundamental and perhaps growing divisions that scar this nation. This was not a plebiscite in which an electorate united around a single cause.
Some of these fissures are not new. There were divisions over judicial reforms that led to mass demonstrations in the early years of this government.
There were also divisions over how to respond to the deadly 7 October 2023 attacks - whether to save hostages or destroy Hamas. The casualties suffered by Israeli reservists in the fighting in Gaza that followed deepened tensions over the exemption of ultra-Orthodox young men from military service.
But has this election put in even sharper contrast the deep fault-lines that lie within Israeli society?
There are the tensions between the religious and the secular, divides not just of faith but of society.
Should Israel's government subsidise religious study? Should some parents sacrifice their sons and daughters to defend Israel when others do not? The ultra-Orthodox now make up almost 15% of the population. Their world-view is poles apart from that of denizens of high-tech, modern neighbourhoods of Tel Aviv.
There are divisions over fundamental politics.
Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party suffered significant losses, but is still on track to be the largest in the Knesset. All this for a prime minister accused of corruption, which he denies; a leader also accused of failing to protect Israel before 7 October, something he will not allow to be investigated.
Some 10% of voters backed the Jewish supremacist far-right: politicians like Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who even as results were being announced was promising to establish Jewish settlements in Gaza.
The Arab parties, which represent about a fifth of Israeli citizens, made huge gains, winning some 15% of the vote, potentially giving them seats numbering in the high teens.
And then there was the opposition bloc, a mix of centre, left and right led by Gadi Eisenkot who fell short of winning the change they wanted - change that many believed was existential for the future of this country.
How these vastly diverging views coalesce into some form of government is now the unenviable task facing Israel's body politic - the choices and compromises they may have to make could involve fundamental decisions about the country's future.
Would Netanyahu be ready to abandon his religious allies and form a coalition with right-wingers from the opposition bloc? Would they be ready to swallow their hostility towards the prime minister and sit in his government?
Is the opposition bloc ready to abandon much of its campaign promises and co-operate with Arab parties to force Netanyahu out of office? Are the Arab parties ready to risk joining a government that could fall within months?
Yair Golan, the left-wing Democrat leader, urged the opposition bloc to form a partnership with Arab parties. "We must no longer accept Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes," he said.
But are the people of Israel ready for such a reality?
Amit Segal, an Israeli commentator sympathetic towards Netanyahu, said the high turnout among Arab Israeli voters "reminded Jews on both sides that, after years of division, they may have to learn to sit together after all".
The risk is that this election, instead of putting Israel on a new path, has instead raised further doubts about what it is that unites its citizens. What are the common factors that bind this complex, varied collection of peoples into one polity?
Autocratic governments, which are growing in number, have long criticised democracies for producing weak and temporary governments, often fragile coalitions that struggle to hold together, let alone deliver what the people wanted.
Israel may now struggle for months to form a government. It might even fail and have to hold another election.
President Herzog acknowledged this risk head on as he prepared to open coalition negotiations: "We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections."
For years, Israel has focused on defending itself against its external enemies. But must it also now be ready to defend itself from perils within, if the divisions writ large by this election become unmanageable?
In another speech, Churchill once said democracy was not just "insurance against dangers from abroad". It was also, he added, "insurance against dangers scarcely less grave and much more near and constant which threaten us here at home".
Can Israel's democracy live up to this challenge?

title: Putin hails Elon Musk’s ‘genius’ amid plans for Russian version of Starlink
content_c:
Vladimir Putin praised Elon Musk’s genius and said he was in touch with Starlink’s controlling shareholder as Russia develops its own satellite communications for its military to use against Ukraine.
The Russian president, speaking at a summit with African leaders in Moscow, was comparing the Earth-orbiting network built by Musk’s SpaceX with Russia’s gradual efforts to build its own Rassvet constellation.
“Elon Musk is a genius, a true genius,” the Russian leader said, according to the Tass news agency. “How many of these [satellites] does he have in orbit? More than 5,000, and we’re only taking the first steps.”
The true number of active SpaceX satellites is estimated at about 10,000, which provide the high-speed internet service that has been the subject of a diplomatic row between Musk, the US and Ukraine earlier this month.
A military version of Starlink, called Starshield, was suddenly restricted one night in the middle of October, preventing Ukraine from conducting medium drone attacks and hampering some of its anti-drone air defences.
Initially, Musk, an ally of the US president, Donald Trump, denied that he had ordered a throttling of the internet connection, before saying at the end of last week that he had closed a loophole in which the civilian Starlink had been used by the military.
Putin appeared to be trying to flatter Musk, whose control of the communications technology has raised questions about the US billionaire’s leverage over the White House and the impact he is able to have on Ukraine’s war effort.
“We are in close contact with our American partners – including Mr Musk – because it is very important, in orbit, not to get in each other’s way and to maintain a certain level of discipline and order,” Putin said.
Starlink does not work in Russia and its use by Russia inside Ukraine was restricted earlier this year. Meanwhile, Moscow has begun to develop an alternative system, though, with an estimated 26 working satellites, its capacity is limited.
Last week, after about 10 days of restriction, Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, announced that “Starlink and Starshield operations have been restored” and that the speeds were “now where they need to be”.
Few believe the issue is permanently settled, with relations between Zelenskyy and Trump fraught in the run-up to the US midterm elections next Tuesday. Trump has also reached out to Putin, agreeing to buy diesel from Moscow early in October in an effort to reduce the oil price before Americans go to the polls.
Zelenskyy said on Wednesday that he hoped proposed trilateral peace talks, involving Ukraine, Russia and the US, would take place between 6 and 10 November in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the UAE, shortly after the midterms.
“We are waiting for the American side. I think that they’ll be ready with all the answers after the elections,” the Ukrainian leader said at a press conference in The Hague with the Dutch prime minister, Rob Jetten.
Earlier, Zelenskyy said he had spoken to Andy Burnham, the UK prime minister, as it emerged that Britain would provide £10bn in extra financing for Ukraine over the next three years – and an immediate £500m for air defence systems.
The additional aid was, Zelenskyy said, “a truly strong and very timely step” that came “as Russia needs to see and feel that Ukraine will not be left alone” as the war heads towards what is expected to be its most difficult winter yet.
John Healey, the UK chancellor, announced the extra funding as part of the government’s annual budget. “The prime minister and I called President Zelenskyy to tell him about our commitments in the budget today. He told us: ‘You’ve made my day’.”
The Dutch government also said it would provide €500m in military support for the winter, and a further €1.2bn in non-military aid, partly to help fund urgent repairs to Ukraine’s utilities and manufacturing.
Kyiv has been relentlessly attacked by Moscow this autumn as Russian forces fail to make progress on the frontlines in the east of Ukraine.
Russia had launched more than 100 ballistic missiles against Kyiv and the surrounding region since the middle of October, Zelenskyy said overnight, hitting power plants and other key targets in an effort to cause a humanitarian crisis in the capital.

title: Dozens of people killed after high-speed trains collide in central Spain
content_c:
Spain: Dozens killed in high-speed train crash
October 28, 2026
We have moved our coverage to a live updates. Please join us here.
At least 68 people were killed after a high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in central Spain on Wednesday morning, regional authorities said.
The collision comes nine months after another high-speed rail disaster killed 46 people, renewing scrutiny of safety on Spain's rail network.
Spain train crash: what do we know?
The Castilla-La Mancha regional government said another 58 people required hospital treatment. Rescue workers continued searching the wreckage for survivors and bodies.
Both trains were travelling from Madrid to Seville. The Renfe high-speed AVE service hit the rear of the stationary Iryo train near the town of Urda in Toledo province some 140km (about 90 miles) south of Madrid, derailing two carriages.
Transport Minister Oscar Puente said a computer malfunction had disabled a safety system at around 8:30 a.m., bringing trains to a halt along a 63-kilometer (39-mile) stretch.
A central control center then gave the Renfe train an "inexplicable" instruction to resume its journey without speed restrictions, despite a stop signal remaining active, Puente said. It collided with the Iryo train at 8:53 a.m.
Puente said the train drivers were not to blame. Investigators were still establishing the speed at impact, he added, although trains could travel at 200 kilometers per hour (124 mph) on that stretch.
Images from the scene showed at least two severely damaged train carriages flipped over on their side after tumbling down an embankment.
The Renfe train was carrying 397 passengers and the Iryo service had 147 aboard, according to the regional government.
Spanish PM Sanchez 'shocked' by 'serious' accident
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said he was "shocked" by the "serious" accident.
"Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations," he wrote on social media. "My affection, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families."
The collision comes just months after another devastating rail disaster near Adamuz in Andalusia in January.
In that accident, a high-speed train derailed and collided with an oncoming train, killing 46 people and injuring more than 150. The incident shook the confidence that Spain has in its extensive high-speed rail network.
The crash was the deadliest in Spain since a 2013 collision that killed 80 people.

title: Fußball-WM: Fifa nimmt offenbar fünf Milliarden Dollar mit Ticketverkäufen ein
content_c:
Turnier in Nordamerika Einnahmen seit Katar verfünffacht – Fifa erlöst offenbar fünf Milliarden Dollar mit WM-Tickets
Der Fußball-Weltverband Fifa hat mit Tickets bei der WM in den USA, Mexiko und Kanada einem Bericht zufolge mehr als fünfmal höhere Einnahmen als beim Turnier vor vier Jahren in Katar erzielt. Die Summe aus dem Verkauf von Eintrittskarten und Hospitality liege bei fünf Milliarden US-Dollar (rund 4,49 Milliarden Euro), berichtete die britische »Times« .
Die Höhe der Einnahmen wurde auf Anfrage von der Fifa nicht bestätigt. Offizielle Zahlen sollen nach Angaben eines Sprechers nach den erforderlichen Prüfverfahren im nächsten Jahresbericht veröffentlicht werden. In Katar hatten die Ticketerlöse bei 929 Millionen Dollar gelegen. 2022 gab es noch 64 Partien, in diesem Sommer waren es durch die Aufstockung um 16 weitere Teams insgesamt 104 Spiele.
Massive Kritik am Ticketverkauf
Die hohen Preise und die Praktiken beim Ticketverkauf für das XXL-Turnier in den USA, Kanada und Mexiko hatten für massive Kritik gesorgt und unter anderem die Justiz in Deutschland und den USA beschäftigt. Durch ein dynamisches Preismodell schwankten die Beträge stark. Bei Verkäufen auf dem offiziellen Zweitmarkt profitierte die Fifa, indem sie pro Ticket eine Gebühr von 15 Prozent vom Verkäufer und vom Käufer kassiert.

description: Viele Spiele, hohe Preise: Die Fußball-WM in Nordamerika war ein Turnier der Superlative. Einem Bericht der »Times« zufolge sollen die Tickets der Fifa fünfmal höhere Einnahmen beschert haben als vier Jahre zuvor in Katar.
author: DER SPIEGEL
content:
Turnier in Nordamerika Einnahmen seit Katar verfünffacht – Fifa erlöst offenbar fünf Milliarden Dollar mit WM-Tickets
Der Fußball-Weltverband Fifa hat mit Tickets bei der WM in den USA, Mexiko und Kanada einem Bericht zufolge mehr als fünfmal höhere Einnahmen als beim Turnier vor vier Jahren in Katar erzielt. Die Summe aus dem Verkauf von Eintrittskarten und Hospitality liege bei fünf Milliarden US-Dollar (rund 4,49 Milliarden Euro), berichtete die britische »Times« .
Die Höhe der Einnahmen wurde auf Anfrage von der Fifa nicht bestätigt. Offizielle Zahlen sollen nach Angaben eines Sprechers nach den erforderlichen Prüfverfahren im nächsten Jahresbericht veröffentlicht werden. In Katar hatten die Ticketerlöse bei 929 Millionen Dollar gelegen. 2022 gab es noch 64 Partien, in diesem Sommer waren es durch die Aufstockung um 16 weitere Teams insgesamt 104 Spiele.
Massive Kritik am Ticketverkauf
Die hohen Preise und die Praktiken beim Ticketverkauf für das XXL-Turnier in den USA, Kanada und Mexiko hatten für massive Kritik gesorgt und unter anderem die Justiz in Deutschland und den USA beschäftigt. Durch ein dynamisches Preismodell schwankten die Beträge stark. Bei Verkäufen auf dem offiziellen Zweitmarkt profitierte die Fifa, indem sie pro Ticket eine Gebühr von 15 Prozent vom Verkäufer und vom Käufer kassiert.
Die Fifa verwies auf die Verfügbarkeit günstiger Eintrittskarten sowie die zuletzt beschlossene Erhöhung der Ausschüttung an die Mitgliedsverbände. »Die Einnahmen des Turniers werden den Fifa-Mitgliedsverbänden beispiellose Ressourcen für Investitionen in den Fußball bereitstellen«, sagte ein Fifa-Sprecher der »Times«.

title: Wahl in Israel: Keine klare Mehrheit, stattdessen Hoffnungen und Frust
content_c:
Nach der Wahl in Israel Keine klare Mehrheit, stattdessen Hoffnungen und Frust
Nach der Parlamentswahl droht Israel eine Hängepartie: Keines der Lager hat eine klare Mehrheit. Premier Netanjahu gibt sich kämpferisch. Seine Gegner sind enttäuscht - hoffen aber weiter auf Veränderungen.
Für die einen fühlt es sich an wie ein Triumph, für die anderen wie ein böses Erwachen. Fest steht heute nur: Die Worte, die in der Nacht den Sieg über die Regierung Netanjahu verkündeten, haben nur eine kurze Halbwertszeit. Zum Beispiel das, was Gadi Eisenkot sagte, der frühere israelische Generalstabschef, der angetreten war, um Netanjahu abzulösen: "Die israelische Öffentlichkeit hat sich dagegen ausgesprochen, dass Benjamin Netanjahu weiterhin als Premierminister amtiert."
Nach einer Abstimmung mit einer derart hohen Wahlbeteiligung wäre es laut Eisenkot ein Fehler, erneut Wahlen abzuhalten. "Es ist unsere Pflicht - meine ganz persönliche Pflicht -, alles in unserer Macht Stehende zu tun, um den Willen des Volkes umzusetzen."
Kein Bündnis hat eine Regierungsmehrheit
Doch, was ist der Wille des Volkes? Es stimmt zwar, den letzten Hochrechnungen zufolge hat Netanjahus Koalition mit rechtsextremen und ultrareligiösen Partnern, keine Regierungsmehrheit mehr. Aber Eisenkot und sein Bündnis sind davon noch weiter entfernt.
So kam es in der Nacht auch zu einem der seltenen Momente, in dem man Netanjahu auf offener Bühne singen hörte. "Hab keine Angst, Israel, denn Du bist wie ein Löwe", stimmte der Mann an, der Israel über 19 Jahre regiert hat, und nun zumindest eine Chance hat, weiter an der Macht zu bleiben. Zuvor sagte er: "Wir haben uns gegen unsere Feinde durchgesetzt - und gemeinsam werden wir uns auch in Zukunft gegen sie durchsetzen."
Unklar bleibt, wen er damit meinte. Den von ihm auch im Wahlkampf immer wieder heraufbeschworenen Erzfeind Iran, der Israel laut Netanjahu auslöschen will, oder den inneren Feind in Gestalt arabisch-palästinensischer Israelis, gegen die Netanjahu und seine Partner im Wahlkampf gehetzt hatten und die immerhin mehr als 21 Prozent der israelischen Bevölkerung stellen.
Enttäuschung bei Netanjahus Gegnern
Nachdem es in der Nacht noch so ausgesehen hatte, als lägen die beiden großen Blöcke in etwa gleich auf, hat Netanjahu inzwischen in den Hochrechnungen einen deutlichen Vorsprung. Für die, die auf ein Ende der seiner Regierung gehofft hatten, bedeutet das Enttäuschung.
So sieht es zum Beispiel Edo Lustig, der extra zur Wahl aus dem Ausland eingeflogen ist:
                
                
                Ich kann nicht glauben, dass es Menschen hier gibt, die für diese extreme Regierung, die diese Zerstörung verursacht hat, gestimmt haben. Ich hoffe sehr, dass es zu einer Veränderung kommt und dass Eisenkot und Bennett und alle Mitglieder des dieses Blocks eine Regierung bilden und all das reparieren, was im Land gerade nicht in Ordnung ist.
Rhetorik als gegnerische Wahlkampfhilfe
Ayyoub Sawalha aus Jaffa hat für eine der arabischen Parteien gestimmt. Sie kommen bei dieser Wahl nach aktuellem Stand der Auszählung auf 19 Mandate - doch ob sie an einer künftigen Regierung beteiligt werden, ist alles andere als klar. Auch Eisenkot hat eine Koalition mit ihnen bisher ausgeschlossen.
Sawalha hat dennoch Hoffnung auf eine neue Regierung und Veränderungen - "damit wir zusammen in Frieden leben. Ich will den Rassismus der vergangenen vier Jahre nicht und hoffe, wir haben es jetzt besser." Er hofft außerdem auf einen größeren Einfluss arabischer Parteien, denn dieses Mal hätten so viele arabische Wähler abgestimmt, wie seit den 1990er-Jahren nicht mehr.
Warum das so ist, erklärte Strategieberaterin Nili Reichman im israelischen Armee-Radio: "Ein Teil der Bevölkerung hat in großer Zahl seine Meinung ausgedrückt und sich gegen die Diskriminierung gewandt, die er seit vier Jahren erfährt und gegen die Hetze der vergangenen Regierung." Der Minister für nationale Sicherheit, Itamar Ben-Gvir, habe zum Beispiel durch seine Rhetorik praktisch Wahlkampf für die arabischen Parteien gemacht und ihnen so die etwa 19 Sitze eingebracht.
Hängepartie droht
Was nun aus den Mehrheitsverhältnissen wird, die sich abzeichnen, ist unklar. Wenn das amtliche Endergebnis feststeht, beginnt Staatspräsident Itzchak Herzog mit den Sondierungen und wird dann den Auftrag zur Bildung einer Regierung aussprechen.
Dass der an Benjamin Netanjahu geht, gilt das wahrscheinlich. Doch ob er eine Regierungsmehrheit zustande bringt, ist offen. Israel droht eine Hängepartie.

title: Магнітна буря 29 жовтня: яка її потужність
content_c:
Магнітна буря 29 жовтня: яка її потужність
Незабаром Землю можуть накрити активні геомагнітні умови та магнітні бурі класу G1.
Сьогодні, 29 жовтня, очікується слабка магнітна буря. Це — з К-індекс 1,7 (зелений рівень).
Про це повідомили Мeteoagent і Британської геологічної служби.
Наразі геомагнітна активність слабка. Втім, вже вихідними на Землю може вплинути потік швидкісного сонячного вітру з корональної діри. Через це очікується підвищення геомагнітної активності до активного рівня, а подекуди можливі слабкі магнітні бурі класу G1.
Найчастіше про погіршення самопочуття під час періодів магнітних збурень повідомляють метеочутливі люди, люди з порушеннями сну, підвищеною втомлюваністю або серцево-судинними захворюваннями, вагітні. У них можуть виникати головний біль, слабкість, сонливість, дратівливість чи проблеми зі сном.

title: Нетаньяху обвинил арабские партии в фальсификации выборов в Израиле
content_c:
Премьер-министр Израиля Биньямин Нетаньяху заявил, что арабские политические силы «украли» результаты парламентского голосования. По предварительным подсчетам, они получили рекордное количество мест, а ни один из двух основных блоков не имеет большинства в Кнессете. «Ликуд» Нетаньяху пообещал передать полиции и службе безопасности Шин-Бет «сотни свидетельств и доказательств», однако пока ничего не обнародовал, сообщает The Telegraph.
В «Ликуде» утверждают, что арабские силы прибегали к «серьезным уголовным правонарушениям»: подкупу, угрозам, насилию, мошенничеству и использованию запрещенного программного обеспечения для мобилизации избирателей. По словам партии, эти силы «поддерживают терроризм и уничтожение еврейского государства».
Партия намерена обратиться и в Центральную избирательную комиссию Израиля. По данным The Times of Israel, комиссия подтвердила, что рассматривает запрос. За несколько часов до заявления «Ликуда» один из её высокопоставленных чиновников в эфире телеканала Channel 12 отверг обвинения в мошенничестве. Израильские СМИ ещё до голосования сообщали, что партия готовит такие обвинения на случай, если Нетаньяху не победит.
После подсчета 85% голосов блок Нетаньяху имеет 53 мандата из 120 в Кнессете. Оппозиционный блок во главе с партией «Яшар» бывшего начальника Генерального штаба Армии обороны Израиля Гади Айзенкота получает 48, арабские «Раам» и «Объединенный список» — 19. Для большинства требуется не менее 61 мандата.
Нетаньяху формально не объявил о победе, но утверждает, что его коалиция получила «решающее большинство» среди еврейских избирателей. По оценке издания, во время кампании он активно играл на антиарабских страхах, а в последний день начал выдвигать необоснованные обвинения в том, что арабы «крадут» выборы, чтобы мобилизовать сторонников.
Оппозиция оказалась перед дилеммой: чтобы избежать новых выборов, ей придется договариваться либо с арабскими политиками, либо с самим Нетаньяху. Оба варианта потребовали бы нарушения предвыборных обещаний. Айзенкот назвал результат поражением Нетаньяху и призвал его уйти в отставку. Президент Израиля Ицхак Герцог со следующей недели начнет консультации с лидерами партий. «Мы должны сделать всё возможное, чтобы избежать еще одного раунда выборов», — подчеркнул он.
Результат еще может измениться: не подсчитаны сотни тысяч почтовых бюллетеней, многие из них — голоса военнослужащих, которые могут улучшить показатель правого блока. Работу над ними должны завершить до конца пятницы.
Выборы в Израиле прошли при практически равном распределении голосов: по данным экзитполов трех крупнейших телеканалов, блок Айзенкота должен был получить 52 мандата, лагерь Нетаньяху — 50, арабские партии — 18. Айзенкот ранее фактически исключил возможность создания коалиции с их участием.
Нетаньяху представлял голосование как вопрос существования страны: накануне он опубликовал сгенерированное искусственным интеллектом изображение ядерного взрыва над Тель-Авивом. В день голосования премьер призвал идти на избирательные участки и заявил о высокой явке среди арабских избирателей и своих оппонентов-левых.
description: «Ликуд» требует расследования и уверяет, что располагает материалами для следователей, но до сих пор не представил ни одного из них.

Выборы в Израиле прошли при практически равном распределении голосов: по данным экзитполов трех крупнейших телеканалов, блок Айзенкота должен был получить 52 мандата, лагерь Нетаньяху — 50, арабские партии — 18. Айзенкот ранее фактически исключил возможность создания коалиции с их участием.
Нетаньяху представлял голосование как вопрос существования страны: накануне он опубликовал сгенерированное искусственным интеллектом изображение ядерного взрыва над Тель-Авивом. В день голосования премьер призвал идти на избирательные участки и заявил о высокой явке среди арабских избирателей и своих оппонентов-левых.

title: Вісім цивільних постраждали через ворожі обстріли Сумщини – ОВА
content_c:
Вісім громадян постраждали через ворожі атаки безпілотниками на три громади Сумщини, повідомив очільник обласної військової адміністрації Олег Григоров.
"Вісім цивільних постраждали сьогодні внаслідок атак російських безпілотників на громади Сумщини. Це жителі Сумської, Шосткинської та Путивльської громад", – написав Григоров у Телеграмі у середу увечері.
За даними ОВА, одна жінка та двоє чоловіків перебувають у лікарнях. Їхній стан стабільний. Медики надають необхідну допомогу. Решта – лікуються амбулаторно.
Триває ліквідація наслідків ворожих атак.

title: Israel election results live: count of absentee ballots under way as coalition talks set to begin
content_c:
Israel election results live: count of absentee ballots under way as coalition talks set to begin
With the final count unlikely to shift results significantly, experts say Gadi Eisenkot’s hopes of unseating Benjamin Netanyahu rest on his willingness to work with Palestinian parties
Final ballots being tallied with results expected to show no clear winner
Hello and welcome to our continuing coverage of the Israeli election.
With 91% of votes now counted, the current results show prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc projected to receive 53 seats, with the grouping of his opponent Gadi Eisenkot on 48 and the Palestinian parties on track to receive a record 19 seats.
The final tally of absentee ballots is not expected to significantly shift the results, and with no grouping managing to reach the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset, Israel could be in for weeks of uncertainty, as both sides try to gather enough support to form a government.
Yair Golan, the leader of the centre-left Democrats, a junior partner in Eisenkot’s bloc, has told Israeli media that he will meet leaders on Thursday for coalition talks. According to the Times of Israel, he will hold talks with Eisenkot, the leading opposition candidate and chair of the Yashar party, and Yair Lapid, the number-two in the opposition B’Yachad party.
This would mark the official start of coalition talks, and Golan has been the only opposition leader so far backing working with the parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel.
Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, voiced hope that the country could avoid a second election. “We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections,” said Herzog, who is tasked with determining which candidate to tap to form a government, urging parties to keep “an open mind”.
Israel’s future hangs in the balance after it became clear that Benjamin Netanyahu has lost his governing majority. His political fate now depends on whether opposition Jewish parties are prepared to forge a common front with Palestinian parties, whose support surged in Tuesday’s historic elections. Indeed, Gadi Eisenkot and his allies face a clear choice: either make a pact with Arab Israeli parties heading for a record result of 19 seats, or hand Netanyahu a political lifeline in the form of new elections or a unity government.
Yousef Jabareen, head of the Arab-majority Joint List, said the Israeli public had voted for new leadership and “anyone who wants to offer a substantive and genuine alternative to Netanyahu’s blood-soaked government will have to talk to us”. He told AFP that while he was willing to cooperate with an opposition-led government to unseat Netanyahu, he was not open to joining such a coalition outright. The ad hoc support of Palestinian lawmakers could enable Eisenkot to maintain a minority government, although few observers believe such an arrangement would survive for long.
Israel’sCentral Elections Committeesaid it had received a Likud party complaint alleging that Arab parties had compromised election integrity and would examine the claims as part of its routine post-election review. Netanyahu’s party responded to partial election results showing Arab-led parties could play a king-making role in forming a new governmentby accusing them – without evidence – of “stealing” the election and demanding that the police and Shin Bet security service investigate the allegations.
UNrights chief Volker Turk has said that he hopes the next Israeli government will“change course massively” and respect international law. “The message is: don’t continue the current course of warfare where you think you are above international law, because I think that’s what we have frankly seen in the current environment,” Turk told reporters in New York. He added: “Israel has its obligations under international law, international humanitarian law, international human rights law, and they need to respect them, and I hope that the next government will do precisely that and change course massively.”
Israel’s left-leaning newspaper Haaretz has published an editorial calling on the country’s opposition bloc to form a government with the Palestinian parties.
With the combined number of Knesset seats for Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc and the grouping of Palestinian parties projected to be 67, the paper writes that Netanyahu’s government has “lost substantial support since the last round of elections.”
The figures clearly point to an unprecedented achievement by the Arab community, which voted en masse for political partnership with Jews. Despite the challenges and reservations about voting, and amidst a particularly racist incitement campaign, a record 19 Knesset seats loudly and clearly declare: We are an inseparable part of this country.”
The editorial goes on to say that there is reason to believe that the leaders of Eisenkot’s change bloc will discard these “19 Knesset seats simply because they belong to Arab voters.”
This would be a slap in the face to the citizens who went to the polls in droves to vote for integration.”
Israel’s choice: Netanyahu remaining in power or a Palestinian-backed coalition
Emma Graham-Harrison
Hours before the final results from Israel’s elections were in, several things were clear. Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition had lost its mandate, and the opposition had a firm majority.
But most of Israel’s Jewish opposition ruled out governing with Palestinian-led parties, in the course of a racist election campaign in which Netanyahu painted Palestinian citizens as an enemy inside the state.
The self-imposed ban on a broader opposition alliance, if it holds, offers Netanyahu the prospect of turning his defeat into another term in office – or at least a prolonged mandate as caretaker prime minister and perhaps another round of elections.
This confected barrier to unseating Netanyahu became the focus of Israeli media and analysts. “No Clear Government” announced the newspaper Israel Hayom. “Road to Unity Government Has Been Paved”, read an article on Channel 12.
Yair Golan, leader of the centre-left Democrats, attacked that framing. “Netanyahu lost. I know how to count,” he said in a statement calling for a government with Palestinians, who make up about 20% of Israel’s population.
“We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes,” he said. “We have a majority. We have a responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a change government in partnership with Arab citizens of Israel.”
While Palestinian-led parties do not describe themselves as Zionist, neither do some of the ultra-Orthodox groups who are a key part of Netanyahu’s current coalition.
A survey taken as polls closed on election day showed that a clear majority of opposition voters supported forming a government with the Palestinian-led Ra’am in order to unseat Netanyahu, political psychology researcher Eran Halperin said.
But opposition leaders were silent on Wednesday, as they apparently tried to balance their desire to unseat Netanyahu with promises against working with Palestinians.
Former general Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the biggest opposition party, has not directly ruled out governing with Palestinians but laid out conditions that made it politically impossible for them to join a coalition.
Palestinians have been clearer about their priorities. “We are ready and prepared to pave the way for the ousting of the Netanyahu government,” Yousef Jabareen, leader of the larger Joint List, said on Wednesday. “The change comes through Jewish-Arab partnership.”
Israel’s elections committee has said it began counting absentee ballots at 1am local time. That count is expected to last until Thursday evening, with an estimated 500,000 ballots from military personnel and diplomats to be tallied up.
They are not expected to significantly change the results.
Under Israeli electoral law, each voter is assigned a specific polling station and can only vote at that station. However in exceptional circumstances, some voters are allowed to cast their ballot at special polling stations they are not registered at. Among those afforded this exception are soldiers stationed at IDF bases, diplomats working abroad, prisoners and prison guards and people in hospital.
These absentee ballots are transported directly to the Knesset where they undergo a series of checks before they are counted, which is why they arrive in the final count much later.
Final ballots being tallied with results expected to show no clear winner

title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
content_c:
Senegal's Youth Olympics bring pride, politics and legacy questions
October 28, 2026
On the final day of October, what may well be the final Summer Youth Olympics ever will begin. It will be the first on African soil as around 2,700 athletes aged 15-17 arrive in Senegal to compete across a total of 153 events in 25 sports.
Hosted in eight venues across three locations – Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly, 80 kilometers (50 miles) from the capital – these Games are seen by many as a prelude to Africa hosting a full Olympics one day in the future.
"I'm really excited about the Youth Olympic Games because, for the first time, I'll be representing our country," 15-year-old judoka Aisha Diop who is competing for Senegal told DW.
"I am very proud to be able to represent my country at these Games. This will really motivate young African athletes because they will improve, and they will want to continue playing sports now that the Youth Games have been held here."
An historic Games for Senegal and Africa
The 2026 Youth Games in Senegal will also be a first beyond the history it is making in Africa.
"Of the 2,700 athletes who will be competing in Dakar, there will be a 50-50 split between men and women," Olivia Nloga, Chief Brand Promotion Officer on the organizing committee, told DW.
"But this parity isn't just reflected in the overall figure. This gender parity will also be reflected in each event and in each sport where such parity actually exists."
Several sports are also making their debut at the Youth Olympic Games, such as five-a-side baseball, kung fu and the Senegalese specialty of beach wrestling. There's also a refugee team at the Youth Olympic Games for the first time.
"As I said earlier, the Youth Olympic Games aren't just about sports, and they aren't just about infrastructure," said Nloga.
"For us, it was also important to use this time to build on and reinforce the idea that these Games in Senegal are a celebration for the people. We did this by investing in culture—for example, through a fashion show and a program called Yi-sol, which is a mural project on the city's walls."
Other projects designed to celebrate the people include music, and a local student designed the mascot. The biggest focus of all though, is on creating sustainability for the young people of Senegal.
"We did so through a program that is very important to us – one that is close to our hearts, namely, the Olympic Civic and Sports Certificate," Nloga said.
"We traveled to schools throughout Senegal and worked with more than 1,000 instructors to reach and make an impact on more than one million young Senegalese children who, during this hiatus, were exposed to and educated about the values of the Olympic Movement."
With recent flooding in the country, there were concerns that infrastructure would have been affected, but Nloga insisted that flood risk had long been in the planning.
"The prime minister held an interdepartmental meeting during which he established a task force to ensure that the necessary arrangements and follow-up measures are put in place to safeguard both the competition venues and the accommodation sites."
Domestic issues remain
With Formula 1 confirming its return to Africa earlier in October, global sport is slowly becoming a more regular event in Africa. As a result though, there have been questions asked about the legacy of such events.
Many in Senegal concerned by the high cost of living and unemployment will see these Games as an unnecessary expense. For the Senegalese authorities though, they are an opportunity for long-term investment in the country's young people as well as infrastructure. There is also the hope that this will make Dakar a major tourist destination.
There was further criticism of the Games being in Senegal from Human Rights Watch (HRW), with the NGO calling on the Senegalese authorities to change their stance on the LGBTQ+ community.
"You are welcoming all of the world. It shouldn't be 'you are welcome to our country, except this, except that,'" Larissa Kojoue from HRW told DW.
"Anti-LGBT legislation and that crackdown that is going on, they contradict the Olympic movement, the Olympic Charter, and also various human rights convention that the country has signed."
Earlier this year, Senegal President Bassirou Diomaye Faye signed into law new legislation on same-sex relations that have proved contentious abroad despite broad political support within the majority Muslim country's parliament. Several human rights groups had voiced concerns about the bill, including warning that it would dissuade people at risk of illnesses like HIV/AIDS from seeking help.
Russia's return to the Olympics
The Games also see the return of Russians to Olympic competition under their own colours after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) lifted their suspension in July. Nevertheless, each sport's international federation can decide whether to authorize the Russian athletes' participation. World Athletics, for example, is upholding its ban, while judo and swimming have allowed Russians to return to competition with their flag and national anthem. According to the Russian Olympic Committee, 13 athletes will compete at the Youth Games in Senegal accompanied by 10 coaches.
Despite the various concerns, there is an overriding hope that the Games will be prove beneficial for all involved.
"What makes the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar special is that they are also rooted in Senegal's extremely strong sporting culture," Nloga said.
"Every evening, when you take a stroll along the Corniche in Dakar, you're struck by the number of people you see exercising, regardless of their age or physical condition. What we'll be offering during these Olympic Games is also an immersion into Senegalese life – into the way sports are just as much a part of Senegalese identity."
Sira Thierij conducted interviews for this article.
Edited by: Chuck Penfold
description: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.
