title: Nach Wahl zur Knesset: So könnte es in Israel nun weitergehen
content_c:
Nach Wahl zur Knesset So könnte es in Israel nun weitergehen
Israel hat gewählt - doch wer das Land künftig regiert, ist unklar. Der Fahrplan zur Regierungsbildung ist durch Verfassungsfristen streng geregelt. Und doch sind mehrere Szenarien nun denkbar. Ein Überblick.
Die Ausgangslage
Die Menschen in Israel haben ein neues Parlament gewählt. Doch am Tag danach zeigt sich: Eindeutige Wahlsieger gibt es nicht. Teilauszählungen zufolge liegt das Regierungslager von Langzeit-Premierminister Benjamin Netanjahu vor dem Oppositionsbündnis seines Rivalen Gadi Eisenkot. Doch beide verfehlen die für eine Regierungsbildung nötige Mehrheit von 61 Sitzen. Die Listen der arabischen Israelis konnten mit 17 bis 18 Sitzen deutliche Gewinne verzeichnen - sie könnten also noch eine wichtige Rolle bei der Suche nach einer Regierung spielen. Doch die Lage ist kompliziert - und mehrere Szenarien sind in Israel nun denkbar. Ein Überblick.
Szenario 1: Koalitionsbildung
Bis spätestens acht Tage nach der Wahl, also am 4. November 2026, muss das amtliche Ergebnis veröffentlicht werden. Innerhalb von sieben Tagen nach Veröffentlichung des Endergebnisses beauftragt Präsident Izchak Herzog einen Abgeordneten mit der Regierungsbildung. Das muss nicht unbedingt derjenige sein, dessen Partei an der Spitze liegt, sondern jener mit der besten Aussicht, mindestens 61 Abgeordnete hinter sich zu vereinen. Regieren wird, wem es gelingt, eine mehr oder weniger breite und stabile Koalition zu schmieden. 28 Tage plus maximal 14 Tage Verlängerung ist dafür im ersten Anlauf Zeit.
Die Parteien dürften also umgehend Verhandlungen aufnehmen, um eine Mehrheit zu erreichen. Die arabisch-israelischen Parteien Vereinigte Liste und Raam haben sich offen für eine Zusammenarbeit mit Eisenkots Block gezeigt. Eine Unterstützung durch die arabisch-israelischen Parteien könnte der Opposition den Weg an die Macht ebnen. Allerdings ist fraglich, ob Eisenkot mit ihnen zusammenarbeiten würde. Möglicherweise würden sich auch nicht alle Oppositionsparteien diesem Weg anschließen. Dies erschwert Eisenkots Weg an die Macht selbst dann, wenn sein Block am Ende vorne liegen sollte.
Für Netanjahus Block gibt es dagegen kaum Möglichkeiten, weitere Sitze dazuzugewinnen - zumal einige kleinere rechtsgerichtete Parteien an der für den Einzug ins Parlament erforderlichen 3,25-Prozent-Hürde gescheitert sind.
Scheitert der erste Anlauf, bekommt der zweite Kandidat den Auftrag. Auch er hat 28 Tage Zeit. Eine Verlängerung ist keine Option. Danach gibt es eine letzte Möglichkeit: Mindestens 61 Abgeordnete müssen binnen 21 Tagen einen Kandidaten vorschlagen. Dieser muss dann innerhalb von 14 Tagen eine Regierung bilden.
Szenario 2: Minderheitsregierung
Sollte es keinem Block gelingen, mindestens 61 Abgeordnete hinter sich zu vereinen, könnte ein Kandidat versuchen, ohne eigene Mehrheit zu regieren. Dabei wäre er auf einzelne Abgeordnete angewiesen. Experten zufolge könnten arabische Abgeordnete etwa eine Minderheitsregierung stützen, ohne dabei Teil einer Koalition zu werden. In diesem Szenario könnten die beiden arabisch-israelischen Listen eine entscheidende Rolle spielen, indem sie der Regierung bei Abstimmungen eine Mehrheit verschaffen könnten. Ein Fünftel der rund zehn Millionen Israelis sind Araber mit israelischem Pass.
Nach Einschätzung des Politikwissenschaftlers Tal Elovitz wäre eine Minderheitsregierung auch unter Eisenkot denkbar. Ihm zufolge deutet eine besonders hohe Wahlbeteiligung unter den arabischen Staatsbürgern "auf einen starken Wunsch nach Partnerschaft hin". "Unterm Strich scheint es derzeit die Möglichkeit zu geben, eine Minderheitsregierung unter der Führung von Eisenkot zu bilden", sagte Elovitz. Doch dies könne sich "je nach endgültigem Wahlergebnis noch ändern".
Sollte sich Eisenkot noch offen für ein Bündnis mit der islamisch-konservativen Raam-Partei unter Mansur Abbas und der Vereinigten Liste überwiegend weiterer arabisch-israelischer Parteien zeigen, dürfte Netanjahu versuchen, ihm diesen Weg zu verbauen. Der Regierungschef und seine ultranationalistischen und religiösen Koalitionspartner dürften alles daran setzen, ein solches Bündnis als illegitim oder gar als Verrat am Staat Israel darzustellen.
Szenario 3: Regierung der nationalen Einheit
Angesichts der extremen Polarisierung in Israel erscheint eine Regierung der nationalen Einheit eher unrealistisch. Doch Kommentatoren spekulieren regelmäßig über eine Parteienkoalition unter Ausschluss der arabischen und ultraorthodoxen Gruppierungen. Laut einer aktuellen Umfrage ziehen 55 Prozent der Israelis ein solches Bündnis Neuwahlen vor, sollte die Wahl keine klare Mehrheit ergeben.
Das Szenario gab es bereits: 2020 einigten sich Netanjahu und Benny Gantz - wie Eisenkot ein Ex-General und Politiker der Mitte - trotz ihrer tiefen Feindschaft nach drei Wahlen innerhalb eines Jahres auf eine Teilung der Macht; sie wollten sich als Regierungschefs abwechseln. Doch das Bündnis zerbrach nach einem Jahr und es wurde erneut gewählt.
Vor der jetzigen Wahl gab es Medienberichte, wonach Präsident Herzog hinter den Kulissen daran arbeitete, Netanjahu und Eisenkot zusammenzubringen, sollte es zu einem politischen Patt kommen. Dieses Szenario würde jedoch auf starken Widerstand auf beiden Seiten stoßen, insbesondere beim Oppositionsblock, der die Wahl als Referendum gegen Netanjahu betrachtet. Eisenkot hatte bereits ausgeschlossen, sich an einer Netanjahu-Regierung zu beteiligen.
Szenario 4: Neuwahlen
Gelingt es keinem Kandidaten, eine Regierung zu bilden, gibt es Neuwahlen. Zwischen April 2019 und März 2021 wählten die Israelis viermal ein neues Parlament, da die Parteien nicht in der Lage waren, sich auf ein tragfähiges Bündnis zu einigen.
Das Parlament löst sich dann automatisch auf. In diesem Fall schließen sich Neuwahlen innerhalb einer Frist von 90 Tagen an. Diese würden dann bis spätestens Mitte April 2027 fällig. Der amtierende Premierminister Netanjahu bleibt bis dahin an der Spitze einer Übergangsregierung.
Quelle: AFP, dpa, AP

title: Москва під атакою безпілотників: літаки з Туреччини розвернули, аеропорти обмежили роботу
content_c:
Москва під атакою безпілотників: літаки з Туреччини розвернули, аеропорти обмежили роботу
У столиці Росії та Підмосков’ї повідомили про атаку безпілотників.
У Москві та Московській області заявили про атаку безпілотників. Через повітряні обмеження в аеропортах кілька літаків змінили маршрут, а частина повітряних гаваней тимчасово обмежила приймання та відправлення рейсів.
Про це пишуть російські пропагандистські ресурси, а також заявив мер Москви Сергій Собянін.
Через запроваджені обмеження в аеропорту «Внуково» два літаки, які прямували з Туреччини до Москви, були змушені змінити курс.
Водночас «Росавіація» обмежила приймання та відправлення повітряних суден в аеропортах «Внуково», «Домодєдово» та «Жуковський» (Раменське). Приблизно за годину обмеження в «Жуковському» скасували, тоді як два інші аеропорти продовжили обслуговувати літаки лише за погодженням.
На тлі повідомлень про атаку Собянін заявив, що російська протиповітряна оборона нібито збила 72 безпілотники, які прямували до Москви. Приблизно о 22:00 за місцевим часом у Московській області оголосили про загрозу атаки дронів.
За даними Astra, у цей період поблизу Наро-Фомінська, розташованого приблизно за 56 км від головної московської автомагістралі, пролунали три вибухи. При цьому звуків безпілотників не було чути. Також серія вибухів лунала в напрямку Калузької області.
Згодом Собянін повідомив про ще 24 нібито збиті безпілотники, які, за його словами, летіли в напрямку Москви.

title: Judge rebuffs Trump DoJ’s bid to force California to set aside 20,000 ballots
content_c:
A federal judge declined to order California election officials to segregate and not count ballots from people the Trump administration claimed were non-citizens, rebuffing a legally thin request from the justice department that appeared designed to cast doubt over the results of the midterms.
The ruling from US district judge David Carter, nominated to the federal bench by Bill Clinton, comes about two weeks after the justice department delivered a USB drive to election officials in Los Angeles and Sacramento that it said contained the names of 20,000 non-citizens on the state’s voter rolls. There are more than 23 million registered voters in California and non-citizen voting is extremely rare.
“This case is about the right of every American citizen to vote in a free and fair election,” Carter wrote in his Wednesday evening ruling. “Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch.”
“In bringing this lawsuit, the Executive would have this Court believe that it reigns as a sole sovereign,” Carter continued. “But California and its people are sovereign, too.”
The justice department gave officials just 48 hours to review the list and said it would sue the state if officials did not sequester ballots from those whose citizenship it could not confirm. The department refused to provide more details about its methodology and Los Angeles officials found preliminary indicators the list was inaccurate. The justice department then sued California on 15 October to try and force the state to sequester the ballots and verify citizenship.
If the justice department’s request were granted, Carter wrote, it would likely violate a 1993 law that requires states to strike ineligible voters from its official lists no later than 90 days before an election.
California election officials have said they cannot verify the citizenship of those on the agency’s list before election day. Carter chastised the justice department’s directive as risking the disenfranchisement of thousands of voters. “A ballot segregated, in effect, would be a ballot removed,” Carter wrote.
The justice department separately has threatened to prosecute election officials in the state if they tabulate ballots from non-citizens. Such a move would be without a legal basis, Sam Trepel, a former prosecutor at the justice department, wrote in a blogpost this month. After filing the lawsuit, the Trump administration began providing lists to other counties of suspected non-citizen voters. When election officials began reviewing them, they found the department had flagged voters who were not on the rolls and had provided insufficient information to verify their citizenship status, according to CalMatters.
Carter’s ruling came after the justice department tried to bypass him entirely. After Carter set a 27 October hearing on the justice department’s emergency motion, the department took the unusual step of appealing to the US court of appeals for the ninth circuit, saying Carter was not considering the case fast enough. A panel of ninth circuit judges ruled 2-1 against the justice department earlier this week.
Legal experts have been skeptical about the justice department’s efforts in California since the outset. In July, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced it had identified up to 190,000 non-citizens on California voter rolls. The DHS did not provide more details to the state until after ballots had already gone out in the state.
“Eroded trust in our democracy is irreparable. Once a vote is segregated, lasting harm has occurred. If the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger,” Carter wrote in his Wednesday opinion. “This Court declines to be a party to such process.”
Uwa Ede-Osifo contribued reporting

title: Berliner Linksfraktion vertagt Entscheidung über Abgeordnete Emde erneut
content_c:
Berliner Linksfraktion Weiterhin keine Entscheidung zu umstrittener Emde
Im Umgang mit der Abgeordneten Emde hat die Berliner Linksfraktion immer noch keine Lösung gefunden. Wie es weitergeht, blieb offen. Emde steht unter anderem wegen ihrer Aussagen zum Existenzrecht Israels in der Kritik.
Die Berliner Linke hat im Umgang mit der wegen ihrer Israel-Kritik umstrittenen Abgeordneten Vanessa Emde noch keine Lösung gefunden. Nach einer Sitzung des Fraktionsvorstandes mit Emde und einer Sitzung der gesamten Fraktion sagte ein Sprecher am Dienstag lediglich, man sehe weiterhin keine gemeinsame Arbeitsgrundlage mit der Abgeordneten. Wie es nun weitergeht, blieb offen. Das werde in den Gremien besprochen und beschlossen, so der Sprecher.
Der Fraktionsvorstand hatte bereits in der vergangenen Woche in einer digitalen Sitzung beraten. Die Neuköllner Abgeordnete Emde, die eingeladen war, hatte sich damals jedoch krankgemeldet und nicht an der Sitzung teilgenommen.
Emde kritisierte Erklärung, die sie selbst unterschrieben hatte
Die neu gewählte Abgeordnete aus Neukölln hatte im Wahlkampf stark auf das Thema Palästina-Solidarität gesetzt und Israel kritisiert. Sie hatte dabei unter anderem erklärt, dass es kein Existenzrecht für Staaten gebe, sondern nur für Menschen. Am 15. Oktober wiederholte sie das in einem Instagram-Video ausdrücklich: "Ich stehe zu meinen Aussagen, und ich nehme keine einzige dieser Aussagen zurück."
Dort kritisierte Emde auch eine Erklärung zum Antisemitismus, die sie wie alle Linke-Fraktionsmitglieder noch zwei Tage zuvor unterschrieben hatte. Darin bekennen sich die Unterzeichner unter anderem zum Existenzrecht Israels. Bereits unmittelbar nach Emdes Kritik erklärte der Fraktionsvorstand, er sehe keine gemeinsame Arbeitsgrundlage mehr mit Emde.
Vorsitzender der Jüdischen Gemeinde Berlins gegen Rauswurf Emdes
Der Vorsitzende der Jüdischen Gemeinde zu Berlin, Gideon Joffe, sprach sich gegen einen möglichen Rauswurf von Emde aus der Fraktion aus. "Wir sind absolut dagegen, denn das, was Vanessa Emde von sich gegeben hat im Sinne der Anklage, dass Staaten kein Existenzrecht hätten, ist absolut korrekt", sagte Joffe im rbb24 Inforadio: "Denn die Existenz von Staaten ist, wenn man so möchte, ein absoluter Glücksfall." Wenn Emde sage, sie sei generell dagegen, dass Staaten existierten, weil alle Menschen leben sollten, wo sie wollten, sei das "eine absolut legitime Meinung", betonte Joffe.
Dennoch habe sich Emde antisemitisch geäußert, so Joffe: "Denn sie konfrontiert Israel schon seit geraumer Zeit mit Völkermordvorwürfen und das ist das Antisemitische." Der Vorsitzende bezog sich damit auf Anschuldigungen gegen den israelischen Staat, dieser betreibe mit seinem Vorgehen im Gazastreifen einen Völkermord an der palästinensischen Bevölkerung. Südafrika hat Israel vor dem höchsten Gericht der Vereinten Nationen, dem Internationalen Gerichtshof in Den Haag, wegen Völkermords an den Palästinensern im Gazastreifen verklagt [tagesschau.de]. Unabhängig davon kommt eine unabhängige Untersuchungskommission des UN-Menschenrechtsrats in einem Bericht zum Ergebnis, dass vier der fünf in der UN-Konvention über die Verhütung und Bestrafung des Völkermordes von 1948 erwähnten Tatbestände erfüllt seien [tagesschau.de].
SPD will Mitgliedervotum über Koalitionsvertrag
Ein mögliches Regierungsbündnis mit der Linken wird in Teilen von SPD und Grünen kritisch gesehen. Verhandler der drei Parteien legten inzwischen aber ein gemeinsames Sondierungspapier vor, das als Grundlage dienen soll. Grüne und SPD billigten die Aufnahme von Koalitionsgesprächen bereits. Bei den Linken muss ein Parteitag am Samstag noch über die Aufnahme formeller Verhandlungen entscheiden. Der Geschäftsführende Landesvorstand der SPD beschloss unterdessen am Dienstagabend einstimmig, ein Mitgliedervotum über einen möglichen Koalitionsvertrag durchzuführen. Im nächsten Schritt ist ein Beschluss des gesamten Landesvorstands notwendig - er solle noch in dieser Woche zu einer Sondersitzung zusammenkommen, teilte der Landesverband mit.
Sendung: rbb24 Abendschau, 27.10.2026, 19:30 Uhr Video: rbb24 Abendschau, 27.10.2026, Sebastian Schöbel im Studiogespräch mit Leonie Schwarzer

title: Туреччина готова відновити переговори між Україною та Росією: Ердоган звернувся до Трампа
content_c:
Туреччина готова відновити переговори між Україною та Росією: Ердоган звернувся до Трампа
Туреччина готова долучитися до зусиль із відновлення переговорного процесу між Україною та Росією задля припинення війни.
Президент Туреччини Реджеп Таїп Ердоган висловив готовність Анкари допомогти відновити дипломатичні контакти між Україною та Росією, щоб сприяти завершенню війни.
Про це повідомила канцелярія турецького лідера в соціальній мережі X.
З відповідною заявою Ердоган виступив під час телефонної розмови з президентом США Дональдом Трампом.
«Президент Ердоган підкреслив, що Туреччина готова зробити свій внесок у зусилля, спрямовані на відновлення дипломатичного процесу між Україною та Росією задля припинення війни», — йдеться в повідомленні канцелярії.
Окрім перспектив відновлення переговорів, лідери обговорили двосторонні відносини між Туреччиною та Сполученими Штатами, а також актуальні регіональні й міжнародні питання.
Раніше повідомлялося, що президент Туреччини Реджеп Таїп Ердоган заявив, що війна між Росією та Україною має закінчитися за умови повного збереження українського суверенітету та кордонів.
Ми раніше інформували, що у Кремлі поставили під сумнів швидке проведення тристороннього саміту Путіна, Трампа і Зеленського.

title: Obama mocks Trump’s response to Cheesecake Factory jibe. ‘They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke!’ – as it happened
content_c:
Obama mocks Trump's response to Cheesecake Factory jibe. 'They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke, not to inflation, but to that joke!'
We are still watching simultaneous rallies, for Republicans in Ohio, and for Democrats in Georgia, that have overlapped in interesting ways at times.
Minutes ago in Ohio, Donald Trump responded his indignation to his predecessor Barack Obama’s joke that “he’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.”
“I paid for it myself. I fixed it, and now it’s more beautiful and in better shape,” Trump said, defending the quality of his renovations to the White House. “President Obama,” he added, was miffed because he is someone “who doesn’t understand cleanliness, who doesn’t understand broken, cracked stone and sidewalk, who doesn’t understand that having asphalt going to your main entrance is not the right thing”.
A short time later in Georgia, Obama repeated his jibe and then reflected on the outraged response to his joke.
“The guy is building a ballroom that is bigger than the White House. He’s paved over the Rose Garden, put a helicopter pad on the South Lawn, and there is gold everywhere. They’re not presenting realistic plans,” Obama said. “These are people who are more interested in performance and flexing and texting and putting people down rather than lifting them up.”
“They enjoy insulting and dividing instead of bringing people together to solve problems,” he added. “I know we’re in Atlanta and I want y’all to know Michelle has love for the Real Housewives. But we got to keep reality TV on Bravo. Leave it to the professionals. We don’t need it in the White House. We don’t need it in the governor’s mansion. We need people like John and Keisha in there.”
In contrast, Trump wound up his remarks by having his supporters watch television – specifically a CNN clip from a month ago that showed he remains very popular with people who describe themselves as “Maga Republicans”. The president did not mention that this clip was taken from a much longer segment that detailed just how unpopular he is with everyone else, including non-Maga Republicans.

'Trump went on the Jeffrey Epstein plane!' heckler shouts at Trump rally in Ohio
Donald Trump is 40 minutes into his remarks in Ohio, where he was heckled over his ties to Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted child sex offender he socialized with for at least 17 years.
During a pause in the president’s remarks, a man shouted: “Trump went on the Jeffrey Epstein plane!” before being removed from the crowd.
“He mentioned Epstein. So I threw Jeffrey Epstein out of a club like 20 years ago, because I thought he was a whack job. That was a great thing I did, I must say,” Trump said. “I threw Jeffrey Epstein the hell out of Mar-a-Lago. And I was the one that was totally exonerated from him.”
While Trump’s aides have repeatedly claimed that Trump banned Epstein from Mar-a-Lago “because he was a creep”, the president has explained the falling out with his old friend differently, saying that the reason was that Epstein “stole people that worked for me”.
Last year, when a reporter asked Trump if one of the people he was referring to was the late Virginia Giuffre, one of Epstein’s most prominent accusers who said in a lawsuit that she was hired away from the Mar-a-Lago spa by Epstein’s accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell in 2000, when she was 16.
Giuffre, who died last year, alleged in her complaint that she was first abused by Epstein and Maxwell together, and then “lent out to other powerful men”, including then Prince Andrew.
“I think she worked at the spa,” Trump replied then. “I think so. I think that was one of the people, yeah. He stole her. And by the way, she had no complaints about us, as you know. None whatsoever.”

“I’ve known Jeff for 15 years. Terrific guy,” Trump told New York magazine in late 2002. “He’s a lot of fun to be with. It is even said that he likes beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side.”
Sarah Blaskey, a Miami Herald investigative reporter, also pointed out in her 2020 book on Mar-a-Lago that Epstein remained on the membership rolls of Mar-a-Lago until October 2007, more than a year after he was first arrested and charged with soliciting prostitution from a minor.

At rallies occurring at the same time, Donald Trump just boasted in Ohio about what he calls the great success of his war in Iran, while Jon Ossoff, in Georgia, mocked Trump for that war and other failures.
Trump made no mention of the fact that the war with Iran he started in February is still not over, and repeated his lie that the war was necessary to prevent Iran from making a nuclear weapon.
“While the crook president and his crook family rake in billions from all over the world, you pay more for everything,” Ossoff told Georgians. “They lied us into war and spent most of the last year covering up for the world’s most famous pedophile.”
“Now remember, they also promised peace. They promised peace. Instead, today marks eight months of a needless war that the useless, draft-dodging commander-in-chief can’t figure out how to end or how to win,” Ossoff continued.
“Remember last year, last year they claimed Iran’s nuclear program had been obliterated? Do you remember that? And then this year, they told us it posed an imminent threat. Both times lies,” he added.
“On day four of the war, day four, the president declared victory,” he continued. “On day 11, Trump said, quote, ‘the war is very complete’. Day 13, quote, ‘we won’. Day 21, ‘getting very close’. Day 32, quote ‘leaving very soon’. On day 40, the president declared, quote, ‘total and complete victory’. Today is day 243. Twenty one Americans are dead and hundreds wounded. Iran still has its uranium and drones and missiles while diesel hits its all time high. They’ve drained our stockpiles to achieve nothing while the president builds himself a victory arch.”
Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens' fiancé says he is voting for Republican Mike Rogers, not Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
Jason Turkish, who is engaged to be married to Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens, appeared at a campaign event for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan on Wednesday and told reporters that he was voting for the Republican, not Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who narrowly defeated Stevens in the Democratic primary in August.
Turkish, a disabilities and civil rights lawyer, said at a Republican Jewish Coalition event for Rogers that El-Sayed’s refusal to say that Iran was a greater threat to the United States than Israel in the first general election debate was “100% disqualifying to be a United States senator”.
Turkish, described by Jewish Insider as “a prominent Jewish Democrat in Michigan”, said that El-Sayed’s rhetoric “makes folks unsafe”.
“When he says genocide over and over,” Turkish said of El-Sayed’s criticism of Israel’s destruction of Gaza, “he makes my community less safe.”
“We’ve never seen a candidate for US Senate act so recklessly toward the safety of Jews in the community as we have from Abdul,” Turkish told the Detroit News.
According to the Detroit News, Turkish has donated Democrats and Republicans, including $200,000 to Democratic candidates in the midterm elections and over $24,000 to support Maine Republican Susan Collins.
Donald Trump is scheduled to speak soon at a rally for Republican candidates in Chillicothe, Ohio, where the party’s nominee for governor, Vivek Ramaswamy, and the sitting senator Jon Husted, have already spoken.
Meanwhile in Georgia, Barack Obama is waiting to address a Democratic rally in Atlanta, in support of the party’s nominee for governor, Keisha Lance Bottoms and sitting senator Jon Ossoff.
Bottoms and Ossoff are scheduled to speak immediately before Obama. The Georgia rally is running about 30 minutes behind schedule, meaning that it is likely that Trump and Obama will be speaking at the same time.
As we watch the simultaneous rallies for in Ohio and Georgia, we are currently being treated to a musical split-screen.
Janelle Monáe is currently performing live in Atlanta, following a performance by the HBCU Clark Atlanta University marching band, while Trump supporters in Ohio are being treated to his rally playlist, which includes songs from a number of artists who sued to have him stop using their music. The crowd is currently listening to Sinéad O’Connor’s version of Nothing Compares 2 U, which her estate said in 2024 she would have been “disgusted, hurt, and insulted” to have used at Trump’s rallies.
During tonight’s rally in Georgia, Raphael Warnock, the state’s Democratic senator, described the upcoming election as a “moral moment in America”.
“There are demagogues at the highest levels of our government who are trying to divide us and distract us in order to dominate us, but we come here tonight to say the jig is up.”
Warnock criticized Republicans in Congress for supporting legislation that will take away healthcare from millions of Americans, and cause 1.2 million children to lose access to Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Snap) benefits. He referenced a photo of Republicans praying before voting on Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
“Our nations leaders, led by the speaker of the House, Mike Johnson, gathered together, put their arms around each other and they knelt down to pray, donning the garments of virtue while literally taking food out of the mouths of hungry children,” Warnock said.
Obama campaigns in Georgia as Trump stumps in Ohio in dueling midterm rallies
With midterm elections less than a week away, Donald Trump and Barack Obama were set to appear at rallies on Wednesday night as Republicans and Democrats make some of their final appeals to voters in key states.
Obama, who was recently in Michigan to support Abdul El-Sayed, is in Georgia, where he will campaign for Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor seeking the governor’s office, and the senator Jon Ossoff.
Meanwhile, Donald Trump, who has appeared at more than 20 rallies in October, was returning to the battleground state of Ohio to support Republican candidates, including Vivek Ramaswamy, who is running for governor, and Jon Husted for Senate.
JD Vance was in North Carolina stumping for Michael Whatley, the former RNC chair, who faces a tough race for Senate against Democrat and former governor Roy Cooper.
Donald Trump continued to rail against Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola, accusing her of “Voter Fraud at the Highest Level” following a report from the New York Times that her campaign recruited a man with the same name as her Republican opponent.
In his fourth social media post on the subject in two hours, the president said on Wednesday that Peltola should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted: “Nothing else will do! This behavior in our Elections cannot be allowed to continue.”
Peltola’s campaign recruited the candidate in order to peel away votes, the New York Times reported.
JD Vance echoed Trump’s criticism. “Even the New York Times admits that Mary Peltola is a total crook who tried to rig the Alaska senate race in her favor,” he said.
JD Vance has reportedly contacted Iran’s security chief in an effort to resume peace negotiations.
The Wall Street Journal, citing US officials and others familiar with the matter, reported on Wednesday that the vice-president sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, the hardline leader of Iran’s supreme national security council, at Trump’s urging.
Vance is seeking to determine whether the countries can “find enough common ground” to deter the president from ordering an attack in the near future, according to the outlet.
The development comes just ahead of the midterm elections, and Trump’s deeply unpopular war threatens to hurt Republicans. The US military has already spent over $47bn on the conflict, more than 25% higher than the defense department’s estimate in the summer, according to Pentagon data first obtained by Reuters.
Trump is bound for Ohio to campaign for Republican candidates in the state. Republicans are defending a seat there in a Senate race that has turned out much closer than might’ve been expected in reliably red Ohio. JD Vance, meanwhile, is campaigning in North Carolina, where Republicans face even longer odds.
Obama will campaign in Georgia alongside local Democrats. Obama will join Jon Ossoff, the Democratic senator, and Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor seeking to flip the Georgia governor’s office, on the campaign stage.
Alaska Democrats intentionally recruited a candidate with the same name as their opponent, according to a new report. The New York Times found that Mary Peltola’s campaign had, despite its public denials, recruited a man named Dan Sullivan to run against the Republican incumbent, also named Dan Sullivan. The revelation prompted Trump to call for Peltola’s removal from the ticket.
Flavio Bolsonaro, the defeated rightwing candidate for Brazil’s presidency, landed in Miami. Bolsonaro had been ordered to turn over his passports in connection with a criminal investigation following his defeat by leftwing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Instead, he fled across Brazil’s border with Argentina and flew to the US, where he’s been granted apparent safe harbor by Trump’s state department.
The US Federal Reserve opted to keep interest rates steady. Despite inflation remaining above the central bank’s target of 2%, its leaders chose to maintain interest rates at their current level.
Trump shared another post to social media railing against Mary Peltola and calling for her disqualification over recruiting a second Dan Sullivan into the Senate race:
“In Alaska, I don’t think Mary Peltola, after perpetrating such a terrible scheme, should be allowed to run, because this is ELECTION FRAUD,” Trump wrote. “The Democrats cheated! They found a man named Dan Sullivan, put him on the Ballot, then lied to the Court, and said they didn’t know anything about it. That’s perjury. She shouldn’t be allowed to run, and neither should the FAKE Dan Sullivan!”
Trump rages at Alaska Democrat whose campaign reportedly recruited man with same name as Republican opponent
Donald Trump responded on Wednesday afternoon to a new investigation from the New York Times, which found that Mary Peltola’s Alaska Senate campaign actively recruited a man with the exact same name as Peltola’s Republican opponent in order to peel away votes.
In a social media post, Trump insisted that Peltola’s actions were illegal (it’s not clear that they were) and that she should be disqualified from the race.
“It has just been determined that the Democrats in Alaska illegally searched for, and recruited, a man named Dan Sullivan to run against our distinguished Republican Senator, Dan Sullivan, in order to defraud, confuse, and obfuscate the Election, thereby taking votes away from the REAL Senator, Dan Sullivan,” Trump wrote on his personal social media account.
The Peltola campaign had, up until now, denied any connection to the campaign launched by the second Dan Sullivan, who just so happened to share the name of Dan Sullivan, the Republican incumbent whose Senate seat Peltola is trying to win.
The Department of Justice has moved to try to block the certification of the Alaska Senate race, should the second, non-Republican Mr Sullivan pull enough votes to shift the outcome.
Trump continued: “The Democrats’ false statements were made under oath in Federal Court. Therefore, they perjured themselves, and should be liable for very serious consequences. Mary Peltola should suffer the Legal and Political consequences for what she has done, A FRAUD ON THE AMERICAN PUBLIC, and Dan Sullivan should be allowed to run without either Mary Peltola or FAKE Dan Sullivan on the Ballot.”

“We seem to constantly just tolerate unseriousness. The people who are currently in charge, they’re not doing their homework. They’re not they’re not doing their work. They’re not presenting realistic plans,” Obama said. “These are people who are more interested in performance and flexing and texting and putting people down rather than lifting them up.”
“They enjoy insulting and dividing instead of bringing people together to solve problems,” he added. “I know we’re in Atlanta and I want y’all to know Michelle has love for the Real Housewives. But we got to keep reality TV on Bravo. Leave it to the professionals. We don’t need it in the White House. We don’t need it in the governor’s mansion. We need people like John and Keisha in there.”
In contrast, Trump wound up his remarks by having his supporters watch television – specifically a CNN clip from a month ago that showed he remains very popular with people who describe themselves as “Maga Republicans”. The president did not mention that this clip was taken from a much longer segment that detailed just how unpopular he is with everyone else, including non-Maga Republicans.
Obama mocks Trump's response to Cheesecake Factory jibe. 'They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke, not to inflation, but to that joke!'
We are still watching simultaneous rallies, for Republicans in Ohio, and for Democrats in Georgia, that have overlapped in interesting ways at times.
Minutes ago in Ohio, Donald Trump responded his indignation to his predecessor Barack Obama’s joke that “he’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.”
“I paid for it myself. I fixed it, and now it’s more beautiful and in better shape,” Trump said, defending the quality of his renovations to the White House. “President Obama,” he added, was miffed because he is someone “who doesn’t understand cleanliness, who doesn’t understand broken, cracked stone and sidewalk, who doesn’t understand that having asphalt going to your main entrance is not the right thing”.
A short time later in Georgia, Obama repeated his jibe and then reflected on the outraged response to his joke.
“The guy is building a ballroom that is bigger than the White House. He’s paved over the Rose Garden, put a helicopter pad on the South Lawn, and there is gold everywhere. So much gold,” Obama said. “This is a fact, I’m not making this up. He, the president of the United States, is spending time super-gluing gold medallions to the mantel in the Oval Office. I am not making this up. He is literally doing arts and crafts while we are fighting a war and trying to deal with out-of-control prices.”
“I heard the president was not happy when I joked over the weekend that he’s got the white House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” the former president said. “First of all, let me get this on the record: I am the father of two daughters. Do you think, could have survived their childhood without going to the Cheesecake Factory?”
“Chucky Cheese and California Pizza Kitchen and the Cheesecake Factory – that was my jam for about a decade,” Obama said.
“The interesting thing about how the administration responded to the speech I gave the other day. They did not dispute what I said about them being directly responsible for rising prices. They did not argue with that,” Obama continued. “They did not deny tariffs were contributing to higher costs for families. They didn’t say anything about that. I accused this administration, based on the facts, that they were engaging in unprecedented levels of corruption. They didn’t say anything about that. The president wasn’t even mad about the Saddam Hussein comparison. That part didn’t bother him, but he was very upset about the Cheesecake Factory comments. He took great umbrage. He said, I didn’t understand the work of the artisans in the White House.”
“It’s all crazy, but this was the really crazy part,” Obama added. “They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke - not to inflation, but to that joke.”
“The White House even called the secretary of the treasury – this is the man who is in charge of the economy, the person who’s supposed to be figuring out how to make your life more affordable, the guy who’s supposed to be figuring out how to lower inflation and reduce interest rates. They told him he should hold a press conference in front of the Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said, to laughter from the crowd.
'Trump went on the Jeffrey Epstein plane!' heckler shouts at Trump rally in Ohio
Donald Trump is 40 minutes into his remarks in Ohio, where he was heckled over his ties to Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted child sex offender he socialized with for at least 17 years.
During a pause in the president’s remarks, a man shouted: “Trump went on the Jeffrey Epstein plane!” before being removed from the crowd.
“He mentioned Epstein. So I threw Jeffrey Epstein out of a club like 20 years ago, because I thought he was a whack job. That was a great thing I did, I must say,” Trump said. “I threw Jeffrey Epstein the hell out of Mar-a-Lago. And I was the one that was totally exonerated from him.”
While Trump’s aides have repeatedly claimed that Trump banned Epstein from Mar-a-Lago “because he was a creep”, the president has explained the falling out with his old friend differently, saying that the reason was that Epstein “stole people that worked for me”.
Last year, when a reporter asked Trump if one of the people he was referring to was the late Virginia Giuffre, one of Epstein’s most prominent accusers who said in a lawsuit that she was hired away from the Mar-a-Lago spa by Epstein’s accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell in 2000, when she was 16.
Giuffre, who died last year, alleged in her complaint that she was first abused by Epstein and Maxwell together, and then “lent out to other powerful men”, including then Prince Andrew.
“I think she worked at the spa,” Trump replied then. “I think so. I think that was one of the people, yeah. He stole her. And by the way, she had no complaints about us, as you know. None whatsoever.”
The president’s claim that one of the employees Epstein “stole” from him, leading to their break, was the 16-year-old Giuffre complicated the timeline. Giuffre was hired away from Mar-a-Lago in 2000, but two years later, Trump spoke highly of Epstein to a reporter.
“I’ve known Jeff for 15 years. Terrific guy,” Trump told New York magazine in late 2002. “He’s a lot of fun to be with. It is even said that he likes beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side.”
Sarah Blaskey, a Miami Herald investigative reporter, also pointed out in her 2020 book on Mar-a-Lago that Epstein remained on the membership rolls of Mar-a-Lago until October 2007, more than a year after he was first arrested and charged with soliciting prostitution from a minor.
As Trump boasts about Iran war in Ohio, Ossoff mocks his claims in Georgia
At rallies occurring at the same time, Donald Trump just boasted in Ohio about what he calls the great success of his war in Iran, while Jon Ossoff, in Georgia, mocked Trump for that war and other failures.
Trump made no mention of the fact that the war with Iran he started in February is still not over, and repeated his lie that the war was necessary to prevent Iran from making a nuclear weapon.
“While the crook president and his crook family rake in billions from all over the world, you pay more for everything,” Ossoff told Georgians. “They lied us into war and spent most of the last year covering up for the world’s most famous pedophile.”
“Now remember, they also promised peace. They promised peace. Instead, today marks eight months of a needless war that the useless, draft-dodging commander-in-chief can’t figure out how to end or how to win,” Ossoff continued.
“Remember last year, last year they claimed Iran’s nuclear program had been obliterated? Do you remember that? And then this year, they told us it posed an imminent threat. Both times lies,” he added.
“On day four of the war, day four, the president declared victory,” he continued. “On day 11, Trump said, quote, ‘the war is very complete’. Day 13, quote, ‘we won’. Day 21, ‘getting very close’. Day 32, quote ‘leaving very soon’. On day 40, the president declared, quote, ‘total and complete victory’. Today is day 243. Twenty one Americans are dead and hundreds wounded. Iran still has its uranium and drones and missiles while diesel hits its all time high. They’ve drained our stockpiles to achieve nothing while the president builds himself a victory arch.”
Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens' fiancé says he is voting for Republican Mike Rogers, not Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
Jason Turkish, who is engaged to be married to Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens, appeared at a campaign event for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan on Wednesday and told reporters that he was voting for the Republican, not Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who narrowly defeated Stevens in the Democratic primary in August.
Turkish, a disabilities and civil rights lawyer, said at a Republican Jewish Coalition event for Rogers that El-Sayed’s refusal to say that Iran was a greater threat to the United States than Israel in the first general election debate was “100% disqualifying to be a United States senator”.
Turkish, described by Jewish Insider as “a prominent Jewish Democrat in Michigan”, said that El-Sayed’s rhetoric “makes folks unsafe”.
“When he says genocide over and over,” Turkish said of El-Sayed’s criticism of Israel’s destruction of Gaza, “he makes my community less safe.”
“We’ve never seen a candidate for US Senate act so recklessly toward the safety of Jews in the community as we have from Abdul,” Turkish told the Detroit News.
According to the Detroit News, Turkish has donated Democrats and Republicans, including $200,000 to Democratic candidates in the midterm elections and over $24,000 to support Maine Republican Susan Collins.
Donald Trump is scheduled to speak soon at a rally for Republican candidates in Chillicothe, Ohio, where the party’s nominee for governor, Vivek Ramaswamy, and the sitting senator Jon Husted, have already spoken.
Meanwhile in Georgia, Barack Obama is waiting to address a Democratic rally in Atlanta, in support of the party’s nominee for governor, Keisha Lance Bottoms and sitting senator Jon Ossoff.
Bottoms and Ossoff are scheduled to speak immediately before Obama. The Georgia rally is running about 30 minutes behind schedule, meaning that it is likely that Trump and Obama will be speaking at the same time.
As we watch the simultaneous rallies for in Ohio and Georgia, we are currently being treated to a musical split-screen.
Janelle Monáe is currently performing live in Atlanta, following a performance by the HBCU Clark Atlanta University marching band, while Trump supporters in Ohio are being treated to his rally playlist, which includes songs from a number of artists who sued to have him stop using their music. The crowd is currently listening to Sinéad O’Connor’s version of Nothing Compares 2 U, which her estate said in 2024 she would have been “disgusted, hurt, and insulted” to have used at Trump’s rallies.
During tonight’s rally in Georgia, Raphael Warnock, the state’s Democratic senator, described the upcoming election as a “moral moment in America”.
“There are demagogues at the highest levels of our government who are trying to divide us and distract us in order to dominate us, but we come here tonight to say the jig is up.”
Warnock criticized Republicans in Congress for supporting legislation that will take away healthcare from millions of Americans, and cause 1.2 million children to lose access to Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Snap) benefits. He referenced a photo of Republicans praying before voting on Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
“Our nations leaders, led by the speaker of the House, Mike Johnson, gathered together, put their arms around each other and they knelt down to pray, donning the garments of virtue while literally taking food out of the mouths of hungry children,” Warnock said.
Obama campaigns in Georgia as Trump stumps in Ohio in dueling midterm rallies
With midterm elections less than a week away, Donald Trump and Barack Obama were set to appear at rallies on Wednesday night as Republicans and Democrats make some of their final appeals to voters in key states.
Obama, who was recently in Michigan to support Abdul El-Sayed, is in Georgia, where he will campaign for Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor seeking the governor’s office, and the senator Jon Ossoff.
Meanwhile, Donald Trump, who has appeared at more than 20 rallies in October, was returning to the battleground state of Ohio to support Republican candidates, including Vivek Ramaswamy, who is running for governor, and Jon Husted for Senate.
JD Vance was in North Carolina stumping for Michael Whatley, the former RNC chair, who faces a tough race for Senate against Democrat and former governor Roy Cooper.
Donald Trump continued to rail against Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola, accusing her of “Voter Fraud at the Highest Level” following a report from the New York Times that her campaign recruited a man with the same name as her Republican opponent.
In his fourth social media post on the subject in two hours, the president said on Wednesday that Peltola should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted: “Nothing else will do! This behavior in our Elections cannot be allowed to continue.”
Peltola’s campaign recruited the candidate in order to peel away votes, the New York Times reported.
JD Vance echoed Trump’s criticism. “Even the New York Times admits that Mary Peltola is a total crook who tried to rig the Alaska senate race in her favor,” he said.
JD Vance has reportedly contacted Iran’s security chief in an effort to resume peace negotiations.
The Wall Street Journal, citing US officials and others familiar with the matter, reported on Wednesday that the vice-president sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, the hardline leader of Iran’s supreme national security council, at Trump’s urging.
Vance is seeking to determine whether the countries can “find enough common ground” to deter the president from ordering an attack in the near future, according to the outlet.
The development comes just ahead of the midterm elections, and Trump’s deeply unpopular war threatens to hurt Republicans. The US military has already spent over $47bn on the conflict, more than 25% higher than the defense department’s estimate in the summer, according to Pentagon data first obtained by Reuters.
Trump is bound for Ohio to campaign for Republican candidates in the state. Republicans are defending a seat there in a Senate race that has turned out much closer than might’ve been expected in reliably red Ohio. JD Vance, meanwhile, is campaigning in North Carolina, where Republicans face even longer odds.
Obama will campaign in Georgia alongside local Democrats. Obama will join Jon Ossoff, the Democratic senator, and Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor seeking to flip the Georgia governor’s office, on the campaign stage.
Alaska Democrats intentionally recruited a candidate with the same name as their opponent, according to a new report. The New York Times found that Mary Peltola’s campaign had, despite its public denials, recruited a man named Dan Sullivan to run against the Republican incumbent, also named Dan Sullivan. The revelation prompted Trump to call for Peltola’s removal from the ticket.
Flavio Bolsonaro, the defeated rightwing candidate for Brazil’s presidency, landed in Miami. Bolsonaro had been ordered to turn over his passports in connection with a criminal investigation following his defeat by leftwing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Instead, he fled across Brazil’s border with Argentina and flew to the US, where he’s been granted apparent safe harbor by Trump’s state department.
The US Federal Reserve opted to keep interest rates steady. Despite inflation remaining above the central bank’s target of 2%, its leaders chose to maintain interest rates at their current level.
Trump shared another post to social media railing against Mary Peltola and calling for her disqualification over recruiting a second Dan Sullivan into the Senate race:
“In Alaska, I don’t think Mary Peltola, after perpetrating such a terrible scheme, should be allowed to run, because this is ELECTION FRAUD,” Trump wrote. “The Democrats cheated! They found a man named Dan Sullivan, put him on the Ballot, then lied to the Court, and said they didn’t know anything about it. That’s perjury. She shouldn’t be allowed to run, and neither should the FAKE Dan Sullivan!”
Trump rages at Alaska Democrat whose campaign reportedly recruited man with same name as Republican opponent
Donald Trump responded on Wednesday afternoon to a new investigation from the New York Times, which found that Mary Peltola’s Alaska Senate campaign actively recruited a man with the exact same name as Peltola’s Republican opponent in order to peel away votes.
In a social media post, Trump insisted that Peltola’s actions were illegal (it’s not clear that they were) and that she should be disqualified from the race.
“It has just been determined that the Democrats in Alaska illegally searched for, and recruited, a man named Dan Sullivan to run against our distinguished Republican Senator, Dan Sullivan, in order to defraud, confuse, and obfuscate the Election, thereby taking votes away from the REAL Senator, Dan Sullivan,” Trump wrote on his personal social media account.
The Peltola campaign had, up until now, denied any connection to the campaign launched by the second Dan Sullivan, who just so happened to share the name of Dan Sullivan, the Republican incumbent whose Senate seat Peltola is trying to win.
The Department of Justice has moved to try to block the certification of the Alaska Senate race, should the second, non-Republican Mr Sullivan pull enough votes to shift the outcome.
Trump continued: “The Democrats’ false statements were made under oath in Federal Court. Therefore, they perjured themselves, and should be liable for very serious consequences. Mary Peltola should suffer the Legal and Political consequences for what she has done, A FRAUD ON THE AMERICAN PUBLIC, and Dan Sullivan should be allowed to run without either Mary Peltola or FAKE Dan Sullivan on the Ballot.”

title: Nachfolge für Steinmeier: Merz beharrt auf CDU-Vorschlagsrecht
content_c:
Nachfolge von Steinmeier Merz bekräftigt Vorschlagsrecht der CDU
Die Debatte um die Nachfolge von Bundespräsident Steinmeier nimmt Fahrt auf. Aus dem Umfeld des Bundeskanzlers heißt es nun: Merz habe noch keine Entscheidung getroffen - und sehe das Vorschlagsrecht bei der CDU.
Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz ist an einem "geordneten Prozess" bei der Auswahl der Nachfolge von Bundespräsident Steinmeier interessiert. Das erfuhr das ARD-Hauptstadtstudio auf der Asienreise des Kanzlers aus seinem Umfeld.
Demnach sieht Merz grundsätzlich das Vorschlagsrecht für das Amt des Staatsoberhaupts bei der CDU. Als größte Partei in der Bundesversammlung habe sie den Anspruch, den oder die Kandidatin zu stellen. Merz habe dazu bislang aber "noch keine Entscheidung getroffen".
Hoffnung auf Person, die viel Unterstützung hat
Die CDU-Schwesterpartei CSU macht sich für die Präsidentin des bayerischen Landtages, Ilse Aigner, als neue Bundespräsidentin stark. Zudem kursiert der Name der CDU-Fraktionschefin im hessischen Landtag, Ines Claus.
Für die Frage, wer Steinmeier tatsächlich nachfolgt, sei die Präsidiumssitzung der CDU am 9. November ein "wichtiger Zielpunkt". Bis dahin will Merz mit den Ministerpräsidenten und Landesvorsitzenden der CDU sowie mit der Schwesterpartei CSU Gespräche über mögliche Personalvorschläge der Union führen.
Sollte eine unionsinterne Einigung gelingen, werde Merz danach das Gespräch mit dem Koalitionspartner SPD und auch mit den Grünen suchen. Er hofft demnach auf eine Kandidatin, die viel Unterstützung der "breiten demokratischen Mitte" hat. Unklar ist, ob am 9. November ein Name öffentlich benannt werden soll - oder erst nach einer noch weitergehenden Verständigung mit den anderen Parteien.
Merz offenbar intern unter Druck
Die Bundespräsidenten-Wahl ist am 30. Januar 2027 in Berlin. Zuletzt galt Aigner als Favoritin für die Nachfolge von Steinmeier. Sie hat starken Rückhalt in der CSU. Aber auch aus der CDU und der SPD kam Unterstützung für Aigner.
Ablehnende Stimmen gegenüber Aigner sind öffentlich nicht zu hören. Trotzdem steht Merz als CDU-Chef intern offenbar unter Druck, das höchste Amt im Staat aus den eigenen Reihen zu besetzen - oder das zumindest sehr ernsthaft zu prüfen.

title: «Битва за ключ оборони Донбасу»: аналітик пояснив, чому найближчі місяці стануть вирішальними
content_c:
«Битва за ключ оборони Донбасу»: аналітик пояснив, чому найближчі місяці стануть вирішальними
Українські військові змогли уповільнити просування російської армії на Донеччині та стабілізувати лінію фронту на Слов’янському напрямку
Силам оборони України вдалося загальмувати російський наступ у Донецькій області та стабілізувати фронт поблизу Слов’янська. Водночас становище на цій ділянці залишається складнішим, ніж у Запорізькій області.
Про це заявив OSINT-аналітик Клеман Молен.
За його оцінкою, на початку 2026 року українські підрозділи залишили позиції в Покровську та Мирнограді. Після цього російська армія задіяла чотири армії на ділянці фронту завдовжки близько 50 кілометрів і розпочала наступ у напрямку Добропілля.
Однак нині російські війська припинили спроби просуватися до західних адміністративних меж Донецької області та в напрямку Дружківки.
У районі Добропілля росіяни переважно використовують тактику інфільтрації — невеликими групами проникають крізь українські позиції. Подекуди такі підрозділи доходять навіть до центральної частини міста.
Молен наголошує, що Добропілля має важливе стратегічне значення в нинішній війні. Потенційно контроль над містом міг би відкрити російським військам шлях для подальшого наступу на Барвінкове, хоча аналітик вважає такий сценарій малоймовірним через потужні українські укріплення.
«Місто має величезне значення для поточної війни, потенційно воно навіть може відкрити шлях для наступу на Барвинкове, хоча це й малоймовірний сценарій, з огляду на міць українських укріплень», — зазначив він.
Важкі бої продовжуються і за Костянтинівку, де протистояння триває вже понад рік. За словами аналітика, позиції сторін у місті значною мірою переплелися, що ускладнює визначення фактичного контролю над окремими районами.
Молен оцінює, що російські війська мають перевагу приблизно на 50% території Костянтинівки, українські сили — орієнтовно на 15%. Ще близько 35% міста залишаються зоною, де складно однозначно визначити, яка зі сторін контролює позиції.
Ситуація на підступах до Слов’янська та Краматорська протягом 2026 року поступово ускладнювалася. Водночас, за оцінкою Молена, у вересні українським військовим вдалося відкинути російські сили від цих міст.
Попри продовження російських наступальних дій, загальна ситуація для України, на думку аналітика, виглядає дещо кращою, ніж навесні.
Однією з проблем для російського командування він називає обмежені можливості для маневру. Російські підрозділи наблизилися до великих населених пунктів і потужних оборонних рубежів, тому подальше просування вимагатиме фронтальних атак.
Молен наголошує, що найближчі місяці покажуть, наскільки ефективно українські сили зможуть стримувати російський наступ у районі Добропілля та закріпити стабілізацію фронту.
«У найближчі місяці стане зрозуміло, наскільки успішно Україна стримує російське просування біля Добропілля і наскільки успішними стануть її спроби стабілізувати фронт», — підсумував аналітик.
Раніше повідомлялося, що російські окупаційні війська змогли проникнути до північної частини Куп’янська на Харківщині та закріпитися там невеликими групами.
Ми раніше інформували, що українські військові проводять на Куп’янському напрямку фронту успішну операцію «Велес», просунувшись на понад 15 кілометрів та взявши в полон понад три десятки російських окупантів.
description: Українські військові змогли уповільнити просування російської армії на Донеччині та стабілізувати лінію фронту на Слов’янському напрямку

«Битва за ключ оборони Донбасу»: аналітик пояснив, чому найближчі місяці стануть вирішальними
Українські військові змогли уповільнити просування російської армії на Донеччині та стабілізувати лінію фронту на Слов’янському напрямку
Силам оборони України вдалося загальмувати російський наступ у Донецькій області та стабілізувати фронт поблизу Слов’янська. Водночас становище на цій ділянці залишається складнішим, ніж у Запорізькій області.
Про це заявив OSINT-аналітик Клеман Молен.
За його оцінкою, на початку 2026 року українські підрозділи залишили позиції в Покровську та Мирнограді. Після цього російська армія задіяла чотири армії на ділянці фронту завдовжки близько 50 кілометрів і розпочала наступ у напрямку Добропілля.
Однак нині російські війська припинили спроби просуватися до західних адміністративних меж Донецької області та в напрямку Дружківки.
У районі Добропілля росіяни переважно використовують тактику інфільтрації — невеликими групами проникають крізь українські позиції. Подекуди такі підрозділи доходять навіть до центральної частини міста.
Молен наголошує, що Добропілля має важливе стратегічне значення в нинішній війні. Потенційно контроль над містом міг би відкрити російським військам шлях для подальшого наступу на Барвінкове, хоча аналітик вважає такий сценарій малоймовірним через потужні українські укріплення.
«Місто має величезне значення для поточної війни, потенційно воно навіть може відкрити шлях для наступу на Барвинкове, хоча це й малоймовірний сценарій, з огляду на міць українських укріплень», — зазначив він.
Важкі бої продовжуються і за Костянтинівку, де протистояння триває вже понад рік. За словами аналітика, позиції сторін у місті значною мірою переплелися, що ускладнює визначення фактичного контролю над окремими районами.
Молен оцінює, що російські війська мають перевагу приблизно на 50% території Костянтинівки, українські сили — орієнтовно на 15%. Ще близько 35% міста залишаються зоною, де складно однозначно визначити, яка зі сторін контролює позиції.
Ситуація на підступах до Слов’янська та Краматорська протягом 2026 року поступово ускладнювалася. Водночас, за оцінкою Молена, у вересні українським військовим вдалося відкинути російські сили від цих міст.
Попри продовження російських наступальних дій, загальна ситуація для України, на думку аналітика, виглядає дещо кращою, ніж навесні.
Однією з проблем для російського командування він називає обмежені можливості для маневру. Російські підрозділи наблизилися до великих населених пунктів і потужних оборонних рубежів, тому подальше просування вимагатиме фронтальних атак.
Молен наголошує, що найближчі місяці покажуть, наскільки ефективно українські сили зможуть стримувати російський наступ у районі Добропілля та закріпити стабілізацію фронту.
«У найближчі місяці стане зрозуміло, наскільки успішно Україна стримує російське просування біля Добропілля і наскільки успішними стануть її спроби стабілізувати фронт», — підсумував аналітик.
Раніше повідомлялося, що російські окупаційні війська змогли проникнути до північної частини Куп’янська на Харківщині та закріпитися там невеликими групами.
Ми раніше інформували, що українські військові проводять на Куп’янському напрямку фронту успішну операцію «Велес», просунувшись на понад 15 кілометрів та взявши в полон понад три десятки російських окупантів.

title: Non-profit group leaks data of more than 40,000 homeland security workers
content_c:
Data identifying more than 41,000 employees and contractors for the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) was released on Wednesday in an unprecedented leak that reveals how the agency is organized. The records, which were made public by the transpaency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets reference operation names, surveillance programs and information on undercover initiatives.
DHS did not immediately return a message seeking comment.
The leaked data unveils the names, phone numbers and email addresses of employees from various DHS agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.
Most of the agents in the leak – more than 21,000 – work for CBP, and about 6,600 work for ICE.
The data also includes job titles, email groups and other details that show which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance jobs, computer forensics and undercover work.
It was made public at a time when DHS, in turn, has aggressively sought to unmask critics on social media, and obtain records on protestors and journalists – even as it moves to keep its own agents anonymous, defending agents’ rights to hide their identities and faces while conducting enforcement.
In a statement, Emma Best, a Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder, said the hacktivist known as “maia arson crimew” developed a search tool for the data that would allow the public to browse it. Best said the tool would “replace anonymity with accountability” and empower journalists, guide public records requests and boost congressional oversight.
The Department of Peace did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but in a statement included with the data, it said that DHS employees “have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs” and that it hoped the data “can be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction”.
The disclosure – which the non-profit data transparency group says draws on information obtained by an entity calling itself “Department of Peace” – is the third government data leak to have made headlines in the past month.
In September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed the theft of a massive trove of data from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including sensitive job details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees. Last week, the defense department was hit with a class action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel.
The Department of Peace in March claimed responsibility for hacking DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors.
Best’s statement said Department of Peace harvested the data from the Okta sign-on service used by DHS. Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to a Reuters query: “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised.”
Reuters could not immediately verify the authenticity of the entire data trove but it was able to match personal information of about six DHS employees named in the leak to credit bureau records and breach data carried by the dark web intelligence platform District 4 Labs. In other cases, Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach.
In several cases, the data tracked information available on DHS employees’ LinkedIn profiles. But in others, the data revealed nonpublic data about internal DHS organization charts or previously undisclosed programs or operations.
